title.zh: 卷七十二 列傳第三十二 文九王
title.raw: 卷七十二 列傳第三十二 文九王 Volume 72 Biographies 32: Wen Jiuwang

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十二 文九王

translations.literal: Biography 32: The Nine Literary Princes
translations.idiomatic: Biography 32: The Nine Literary Princes

sentences.zh: 文帝十九男：元皇后生劭，潘淑妃生濬，路淑媛生孝武帝，吳淑儀生南平王鑠，高脩儀生廬陵昭王紹，殷脩華生竟陵王誕，曹婕妤生建平宣簡王宏，陳脩容生東海王禕，謝容華生晉熙王昶，江脩儀生武昌王渾，沈婕妤生明帝，楊脩儀生建安王休仁，邢美人生晉平王休祐，蔡美人生海陵王休茂，董美人生鄱陽哀王休業，顏美人生臨慶沖王休倩，陳美人生新野懷王夷父，荀美人生桂陽王休範，羅美人生巴陵哀王休若。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had nineteen sons: the Yuan Empress bore Shao; Consort Pan bore Jun; Lady Lu bore Emperor Xiaowu; Lady Wu bore Prince Shuo of Nanping; Lady Gao bore Prince Zhao of Luling; Lady Yin bore Prince Dan of Jingling; Lady Cao bore Prince Hong, posthumously Xuanjian of Pingping; Lady Chen bore Prince Yi of Donghai; Lady Xie bore Prince Chang of Jinxi; Lady Jiang bore Prince Hun of Wuchang; Lady Shen bore Emperor Ming; Lady Yang bore Prince Xiuren of Jian'an; Lady Xing bore Prince Xiuyou of Jinping; Lady Cai bore Prince Xiumao of Hailing; Lady Dong bore Prince Xieye of Poyang; Lady Yan bore Prince Xiuqian of Linqing; Lady Chen bore Prince Yifu of Xinye; Lady Xun bore Prince Xiufan of Guiyang; Lady Luo bore Prince Xiuruo of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen fathered nineteen sons. The Yuan Empress gave birth to Shao; Consort Pan to Jun; Lady Lu to the future Emperor Xiaowu; Lady Wu to Prince Shuo of Nanping; Lady Gao to Prince Zhao of Luling; Lady Yin to Prince Dan of Jingling; Lady Cao to Prince Hong of Pingping (later honored as Xuanjian); Lady Chen to Prince Yi of Donghai; Lady Xie to Prince Chang of Jinxi; Lady Jiang to Prince Hun of Wuchang; Lady Shen to the future Emperor Ming; Lady Yang to Prince Xiuren of Jian'an; Lady Xing to Prince Xiuyou of Jinping; Lady Cai to Prince Xiumao of Hailing; Lady Dong to Prince Xieye of Poyang; Lady Yan to Prince Xiuqian of Linqing; Lady Chen to Prince Yifu of Xinye; Lady Xun to Prince Xiufan of Guiyang; and Lady Luo to Prince Xiuruo of Baling.

sentences.zh: 劭、濬、誕、禕、渾、休茂、休範別有傳。

translations.literal: Shao, Jun, Dan, Yi, Hun, Xiumao, and Xiufan have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, Jun, Dan, Yi, Hun, Xiumao, and Xiufan are treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 紹出繼廬陵孝獻王義真。

translations.literal: Shao was given in adoption to succeed Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was sent out to succeed Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 南平穆王鑠，字休玄，文帝第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Nanping, Shuo, courtesy name Xiuxuan, was the fourth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu of Nanping, Shuo—courtesy name Xiuxuan—was Emperor Wen's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十七年，都督湘州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、湘州刺史，不之鎮，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia he was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Xiang Province, General Who Crowns the Army, and Inspector of Xiangzhou; he did not go to his post but instead took charge of the garrison at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia he was appointed to command Xiang Province as General Who Crowns the Army and inspector, but he never took up the post and remained in charge of the Shitou garrison instead.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷使持節、都督南豫、豫、司、雍、秦、并六州諸軍事、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in the six provinces of Southern Yu, Yu, Si, Yong, Qin, and Bing, and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he was promoted to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, commander of six provinces (Southern Yu, Yu, Si, Yong, Qin, and Bing), and inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時太祖方事外略，乃罷南豫併壽陽，即以鑠為豫州刺史，尋領安蠻校尉，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Ancestor was pursuing external campaigns, so Southern Yu was abolished and merged into Shouyang; Shuo was then made Inspector of Yuzhou, soon thereafter also took the post of Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and was granted one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: While the Grand Ancestor was pressing external campaigns, Southern Yuzhou was abolished and folded into Shouyang; Shuo became inspector of Yu, soon added the post of Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and received a full set of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，進號平西將軍，讓不拜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West but declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he was offered the title General Who Pacifies the West and declined it.

sentences.zh: 索虜大帥托跋燾南侵陳、潁，遂圍汝南懸瓠城。

translations.literal: The great chief of the Northern Wei, Tuoba Tao, invaded south into Chen and Ying and then besieged the city of Xuanhu in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei warlord Tuoba Tao marched south into Chen and Ying and laid siege to Xuanhu in Runan.

sentences.zh: 行汝南太守陳憲保城自固，賊晝夜攻圍之，憲且守且戰，矢石無時不交。

translations.literal: The acting Administrator of Runan, Chen Xian, held the city and strengthened its defenses; the enemy attacked day and night, and Xian both defended and fought, with arrows and stones exchanged without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The acting Runan administrator Chen Xian locked down the city. The enemy assaulted it day and night; Xian fought as he held, and arrows and stones never stopped flying.

sentences.zh: 虜多作高樓，施弩以射城內，飛矢雨下，城中負戶以汲。

translations.literal: The barbarians built many tall towers and mounted crossbows to shoot into the city; arrows fell like rain, and within the city men carried door-shields to draw water.
translations.idiomatic: The invaders raised tall siege towers and shot into the city with crossbows until arrows fell like rain; inside, men had to carry door panels as shields just to draw water.

sentences.zh: 又毀佛浮圖，取金像以為大鉤，施之衝車端，以牽樓堞。

translations.literal: They also destroyed Buddhist pagodas, took golden images to make great hooks, fixed them on the ends of battering-rams, and used them to pull down battlements.
translations.idiomatic: They tore down Buddhist pagodas, forged the gilt statues into great hooks on the battering-rams, and used them to wrench down the parapets.

sentences.zh: 城內有一沙門，頗有機思，輒設奇以應之。

translations.literal: Within the city was a monk of considerable ingenuity who constantly devised strange countermeasures.
translations.idiomatic: A monk inside the walls, quick-witted and resourceful, kept answering each stratagem with another of his own.

sentences.zh: 賊多作蝦蟆車以填塹，因薄攻城。

translations.literal: The enemy built many 'toad carts' to fill the moat and then pressed close to storm the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy built many 'toad carts' to fill the ditches and pressed in close for a wall assault.

sentences.zh: 憲督厲將士，固女墻而戰。

translations.literal: Xian urged on the officers and men and fought along the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: Xian roused his officers and men and fought them along the breastwork.

sentences.zh: 賊之死者，屍與城等，遂登屍以陵城，短兵相接；

translations.literal: The enemy dead were piled as high as the walls; they climbed the corpses to scale the city, and close combat ensued;
translations.idiomatic: So many enemy dead piled up that they equaled the wall height; the attackers climbed the bodies to reach the ramparts and closed for hand-to-hand fighting;

sentences.zh: 憲銳氣愈奮，戰士無不一當百，殺傷萬計，汝水為之不流。

translations.literal: Xian's fighting spirit grew fiercer; no warrior failed to match a hundred, casualties numbered in the tens of thousands, and the Ru River ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's spirit only sharpened; every defender fought as ten, casualties mounted into the tens of thousands, and the Ru River was choked with the dead.

sentences.zh: 相拒四十餘日，鑠遣安蠻司馬劉康祖與寧朔將軍臧質救之，虜燒攻具走。

translations.literal: After more than forty days of stalemate, Shuo sent the Pacification of Barbarians Army Aide Liu Kangzu and the General Who Pacifies the North Zang Zhi to the rescue; the barbarians burned their siege equipment and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After more than forty days, Shuo sent Liu Kangzu and General Zang Zhi to relieve the city; the invaders burned their engines and fled.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大舉北伐，諸蕃竝出師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year a great northern expedition was launched and all the princely domains sent out troops.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 the court launched a major northern campaign and every princely fief marched.

sentences.zh: 鑠遣中兵參軍胡盛之出汝南，到坦之出上蔡，向長社，長社戍主魯爽委城奔走。

translations.literal: Shuo sent Army Aide Hu Shengzhi out through Runan and Dao Tanzhi out through Shangcai toward Changshe; Lu Shuang, the garrison commander of Changshe, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo sent Hu Shengzhi through Runan and Dao Tanzhi through Shangcai toward Changshe; the garrison commander Lu Shuang abandoned the city and ran.

sentences.zh: 既克長社，遣幢主王陽兒、張略等進據小索。

translations.literal: After Changshe had been taken, he sent the standard commanders Wang Yang'er, Zhang Lue, and others to advance and occupy Xiaosuo.
translations.idiomatic: After Changshe fell, Wang Yang'er, Zhang Lue, and others were sent on to occupy Xiaosuo.

sentences.zh: 偽豫州刺史僕蘭於大索率步騎二千攻陽兒，陽兒擊大破之。

translations.literal: The false Inspector of Yuzhou Pulan at Dasuo led two thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Yang'er; Yang'er struck and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei inspector Pulan brought two thousand horse and foot against Yang'er at Dasuo; Yang'er smashed his force.

sentences.zh: 到坦之等進向大索，滎陽民鄭德玄、張和各起義以應坦之，僕蘭奔虎牢。

translations.literal: Dao Tanzhi and others advanced on Dasuo; Zheng Dexuan and Zhang He, commoners of Xingyang, each rose in support of Tanzhi, and Pulan fled to Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Tanzhi marched on Dasuo; Zheng Dexuan and Zhang He, commoners of Xingyang, rose to join him, and Pulan fled to Hulao.

sentences.zh: 會王陽兒等至，即據大索，因向虎牢，鑠又遣安蠻司馬劉康祖繼坦之。

translations.literal: When Wang Yang'er and the others arrived they seized Dasuo and pressed on toward Hulao; Shuo again sent the Pacification of Barbarians Army Aide Liu Kangzu to follow Tanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yang'er arrived, took Dasuo, and moved on Hulao; Shuo sent Liu Kangzu after Tanzhi.

sentences.zh: 虜永昌王宜勤庫仁真救虎牢，坦之敗走。

translations.literal: The barbarian Prince Yongchang Yiqin Kurenzhen came to relieve Hulao, and Tanzhi was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongchang Yiqin Kurenzhen relieved Hulao; Tanzhi was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 虜乘勝逕進，於尉氏津逢康祖，康祖戰敗見殺。

translations.literal: The barbarians pressed their victory straight forward; at the Wei County ford they met Kangzu, who was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The victors pressed on; at the Wei County crossing they met Kangzu, defeated him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 賊進脅壽陽，因東過與燾會於江上。

translations.literal: The rebels advanced to threaten Shouyang, then passed eastward to join Tao on the river.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy threatened Shouyang, then marched east to join Tao on the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 二十八年夏，虜荊州刺史魯爽及弟秀等，率部曲詣鑠歸順。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-eighth year, the captive Jingzhou Inspector Lu Shuang, together with his younger brother Xiu and others, led their followers to Shuo and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Yuanjia 28, Lu Shuang, Inspector of Jingzhou among the northern captives, and his younger brother Xiu led their followers to Shuo and submitted.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，鑠所生吳淑儀薨，鑠歸京師，葬畢，還攝本任。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year, Wu Shuyi, Shuo's birth mother, died. Shuo returned to the capital, and after the burial was completed, he went back to provisionally hold his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year, Shuo's birth mother, Wu Shuyi, died. Shuo returned to the capital and, after the burial, went back to resume his post provisionally.

sentences.zh: 時江夏王義恭領南兗州刺史，鎮盱眙。

translations.literal: At the time, Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, concurrently held the inspectorship of Southern Yan Province and was stationed at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, held the inspectorship of Southern Yan Province and was stationed at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，還京師。

translations.literal: When he encountered mourning for his mother, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he returned to the capital for mourning.

sentences.zh: 上以兗土彫荒，罷南兗併南徐州，當別置淮南都督住盱眙，開創屯田，應接遠近，欲以授鑠。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering the territory of Yan depleted and desolate, abolished Southern Yan and merged it into Southern Xu Province, and planned separately to establish a Huainan commandant stationed at Xuyi to open military colonies and respond to near and far; he intended to grant this to Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yan territory was depleted, the emperor abolished Southern Yan and merged it into Southern Xu Province. He planned to establish a separate Huainan command at Xuyi, opening military colonies and responding to affairs near and far, and intended to give it to Shuo.

sentences.zh: 既而改授散騎常侍、撫軍將軍，領兵戍石頭。

translations.literal: Before long, he was instead appointed Cavalier Regular Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army, and led troops to garrison Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was instead appointed Cavalier Regular Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army, and led troops to garrison Shitou.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，以為中軍將軍，護軍、常侍如故。

translations.literal: When the usurper seized the throne by regicide, Shuo was made General of the Central Army, with his posts as Protector of the Army and Regular Attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurper's regicide, Shuo was named General of the Central Army while keeping his posts as Protector of the Army and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖入討，劭屯兵京邑，使鑠巡行撫勞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu marched in to punish him, Shao massed troops in the capital and had Shuo tour the lines to comfort the men.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched east to punish the usurper, Shao kept his army in the capital and sent Shuo to tour the camps and hearten the troops.

sentences.zh: 劭還立南兗，以鑠為使持節、都督南兗、徐、兗、青、冀、幽六州諸軍事、征北將軍、開府儀同三司、南兗州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Shao restored Southern Yan and appointed Shuo Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of six provinces, General Who Conquers the North, with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Southern Yan, his Regular Attendancy unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Shao re-established Southern Yan and made Shuo Bearer of the Staff, commander of six provinces, General Who Conquers the North, with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 柳元景至新亭，劭親自攻之，挾鑠自隨。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuanjing reached Xinting, Shao attacked in person and took Shuo with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuanjing reached Xinting, Shao attacked in person and kept Shuo at his side.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭南奔，使鑠守東府，以腹心防之。

translations.literal: When Prince Jiangxia Yigong fled south, Shao had Shuo guard the Eastern Palace and posted trusted men to watch him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jiangxia Yigong fled south, Shao set Shuo to guard the Eastern Palace and posted trusted men to watch him.

sentences.zh: 進授侍中、驃騎將軍、錄尚書事，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Regular Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Regular Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 劭迎蔣侯神於宮內，疏世祖年諱，厭祝祈請，假授位號，使鑠造策文。

translations.literal: Shao welcomed the spirit of Lord Jiang into the palace, listed the taboo years of Emperor Xiaowu, performed suppressive rites and prayers, and conferred false titles, having Shuo draft the appointment documents.
translations.idiomatic: Shao brought the spirit of Lord Jiang into the palace, wrote out Emperor Xiaowu's taboo years, performed curse-rites and prayers, and had Shuo draft the bogus appointment edicts.

sentences.zh: 及義軍入宮，鑠與濬俱歸世祖，濬即伏法，上迎鑠入營。

translations.literal: When the loyal army entered the palace, Shuo and Jun both came over to Emperor Xiaowu; Jun was immediately executed, and the Emperor received Shuo into camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyalists took the palace, Shuo and Jun both defected to Emperor Xiaowu; Jun was executed at once, and the Emperor welcomed Shuo into camp.

sentences.zh: 當時倉卒失國璽，事寧，更鑄給之。

translations.literal: In the haste of the moment the imperial seal was lost; when affairs were settled a new one was cast and given to him.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seal was lost in the turmoil; after order returned a new one was cast for him.

sentences.zh: 進侍中、司空，領兵置佐，以國哀未闋，讓侍中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Regular Attendant and Minister of Works, with military staff assigned; because the national mourning had not ended, he declined the Regular Attendancy.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant and Minister of Works with military staff, but declined the Regular Attendancy while the court was still in mourning.

sentences.zh: 鑠素不推事世祖，又為元兇所任，上乃以藥內食中毒殺之，時年二十三，追贈侍中、司徒。

translations.literal: Shuo had never favored Emperor Xiaowu and had also been employed by the usurper; the Emperor therefore poisoned him in his food. He was twenty-three. Posthumously he was given Regular Attendant and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo had never backed Emperor Xiaowu and had served the usurper; the Emperor had him poisoned at table. He was twenty-three. Posthumously he received Regular Attendant and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三子：敬猷、敬淵、敬先。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Jingyou, Jingyuan, and Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: His three sons were Jingyou, Jingyuan, and Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 敬猷嗣，官至黃門郎。

translations.literal: Jingyou succeeded him and rose to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyou succeeded him and reached Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 敬淵初封南安縣侯，官至後軍將軍。

translations.literal: Jingyuan was first enfeoffed Marquis of Nan'an and rose to General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan was first made Marquis of Nan'an and rose to General of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 敬先繼廬陵王紹。

translations.literal: Jingxian succeeded Prince Shao of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian succeeded Prince Shao of Luling.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和末，召鑠妃江氏入宮，使左右於前逼迫之，江氏不受命。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jinghe era of the Deposed Emperor, Prince Shuo's consort Lady Jiang was summoned to the palace; attendants were made to force her in his presence, but Lady Jiang refused.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Deposed Emperor's Jinghe reign, Lady Jiang, consort of Prince Shuo, was summoned to the palace and pressed by attendants before the throne; she refused.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「若不從，當殺汝三子。」

translations.literal: They said to her: 'If you do not obey, your three sons will be killed.'
translations.idiomatic: They told her: 'If you refuse, we will kill your three sons.'

sentences.zh: 江氏猶不肯。

translations.literal: Lady Jiang still would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiang still refused.

sentences.zh: 於是遣使於第殺敬猷、敬淵、敬先，鞭江氏一百。

translations.literal: Thereupon envoys were sent to their residence to kill Jingyou, Jingyuan, and Jingxian, and Lady Jiang was flogged one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to the residence to kill all three sons, and Lady Jiang was flogged a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 其夕廢帝亦殞。

translations.literal: That same evening the Deposed Emperor also died.
translations.idiomatic: That same night the Deposed Emperor died as well.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追贈敬猷侍中，諡曰懷王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Jingyou was posthumously given Regular Attendant and the posthumous title Prince Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong succeeded, Jingyou was posthumously made Regular Attendant with the title Prince Huai.

sentences.zh: 追贈敬淵黃門侍郎，諡曰悼侯。

translations.literal: Jingyuan was posthumously made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate with the posthumous title Marquis Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan was posthumously made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, posthumous title Marquis Dao.

sentences.zh: 改封孝武帝第十八子臨賀王子產字孝仁為南平王，繼鑠後，未拜，被殺。

translations.literal: The eighteenth son of Emperor Xiaowu, Prince Zichan of Linhe, courtesy name Xiaoren, was transferred to be Prince of Nanping to succeed Shuo; before he could receive appointment he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's eighteenth son, Prince Zichan of Linhe (Xiaoren), was reassigned as Prince of Nanping to succeed Shuo but was killed before taking up the title.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，立晉平王休祐第七子宣曜為南平王繼鑠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi, the seventh son of Prince Xiuyou of Jinping, Xuanyao, was established as Prince of Nanping to succeed Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi, Xuanyao, seventh son of Prince Xiuyou of Jinping, was made Prince of Nanping to succeed Shuo.

sentences.zh: 休祐死，宣曜被廢還本。

translations.literal: When Xiuyou died, Xuanyao was deposed and returned to his original status.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiuyou's death, Xuanyao was deposed and sent back to his original rank.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽元年，立衡陽恭王嶷第二子伯玉為南平王繼鑠，後官至給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui of the Later Deposed Emperor, Boyu, second son of Prince Gong of Hengyang, was established as Prince of Nanping to succeed Shuo and later reached Supervisor in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 1 of the Later Deposed Emperor, Boyu, second son of Prince Gong of Hengyang, succeeded Shuo as Prince of Nanping and later became Supervisor in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，謀反誅，國除。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he plotted rebellion and was executed; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 he plotted rebellion, was executed, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 建平宣簡王宏，字休度，文帝第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xuanjian of Pingping, Hong, courtesy name Xiudu, was the seventh son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuanjian of Pingping, Hong—courtesy name Xiudu—was Emperor Wen's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 早喪母。

translations.literal: He lost his mother early.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died while he was young.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年，年十一，封建平王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingping with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, at eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingping with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 少而閑素，篤好文籍。

translations.literal: From youth he was quiet and plain, and deeply loved literature.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was quiet and unadorned, with a deep love of books.

sentences.zh: 太祖寵愛殊常，為立第於雞籠山，盡山水之美。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor favored him beyond measure, built him a mansion on Cock Cage Mountain with every beauty of landscape.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor doted on him unusually, building him a mansion on Cock Cage Mountain in the finest scenery.

sentences.zh: 建平國職，高他國一階。

translations.literal: The offices of the Pingping state were one rank higher than those of other states.
translations.idiomatic: Pingping's state offices ranked one step above other princely states.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，為中護軍，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he became General Who Protects the Army and took charge of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he became General Who Protects the Army and commanded the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 出為征虜將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，徵為中書令，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was recalled as Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he was recalled as Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，以宏為左將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When the usurper seized the throne by regicide, Hong was made General of the Left and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the regicide, Hong was made General of the Left and Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 又以為散騎常侍、鎮軍將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also made Regular Attendant, General Who Guards the Army, and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named Regular Attendant, General Who Guards the Army, and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖入討，劭錄宏殿內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu marched in to punish him, Shao kept Hong confined in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched east, Shao kept Hong under house arrest in the palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖先嘗以一手板與宏，宏遣左右親信周法道齎手板詣世祖。

translations.literal: The Emperor had once given Hong a hand-board; Hong sent his trusted attendant Zhou Fadao to deliver the hand-board to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu had once given Hong a hand-board; Hong sent his confidant Zhou Fadao to carry it to him.

sentences.zh: 事平，以為尚書左僕射，使奉迎太后，還加中軍將軍，中書監，僕射如故。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and sent to welcome the Empress Dowager; on return he was further made General of the Central Army and Director of the Secretariat, his vice-directorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and went to welcome the Empress Dowager; on return he added General of the Central Army and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臧質為逆，宏以仗士五十人入六門。

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi rebelled, Hong entered the Six Gates with fifty armed guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi rebelled, Hong entered the Six Gates with fifty armed guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 為人謙儉周慎，禮賢接士，明曉政事，上甚信仗之。

translations.literal: In person he was humble, frugal, and careful, honored the worthy and received scholars, understood government clearly, and the Emperor trusted and relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Humble, frugal, and careful, he honored worthies and welcomed scholars, understood government well, and the Emperor trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時普責百官讜言，宏議曰：

translations.literal: At that time all officials were broadly required to offer candid advice; Hong submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the court demanded candid counsel from every official, Hong submitted this memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞建國之道咸殊，興王之政不一。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the ways of founding a state differ, and the policies of raising a royal house are not one.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that every founding age has its own way, and no two dynasties govern alike.

sentences.zh: 至於開諫致寧，防口取禍，固前王同軌，後主共則。

translations.literal: As for opening the path of remonstrance to bring peace and shutting mouths to invite disaster, this is a single track for former kings and a shared rule for later rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet opening the road of remonstrance brings peace, while silencing speech invites ruin—former kings walked the same path, and later rulers share the same warning.

sentences.zh: 秦、殷之敗，語戮刺亡；

translations.literal: The fall of Qin and Yin came from punishing speech and killing those who remonstrated;
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Yin fell because they punished speech and killed remonstrators;

sentences.zh: 周、漢之盛，謗升箴顯。

translations.literal: the glory of Zhou and Han rose as slander became admonition and remonstrance shone forth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han flourished when slander became counsel and frank speech was honored.

sentences.zh: 陛下以至德神臨，垂精思治，進儒禮而崇寬教，哀獄法而黜嚴刑，表忠行而舉貞節，辟處士而求賢異，修廢官而出滯賞，撤天膳而重農食，禁貴遊而弛榷酤，通山澤而易關梁，固已海內仰道，天下知德。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with supreme virtue presiding in spirit, bends your mind to good government: advancing Confucian ritual and exalting lenient teaching, pitying penal law and dismissing harsh punishment, displaying loyal conduct and promoting steadfast integrity, summoning recluses and seeking unusual talent, restoring abolished offices and releasing stagnant rewards, withdrawing the imperial table to value farmers' food, forbidding noble excursions and relaxing the salt and wine monopoly, opening mountains and marshes and easing passes and bridges—you have already made the realm look up to the Way and the world know your virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules with supreme virtue and bent thought on good government: advancing Confucian ritual, lightening punishments, honoring loyalty, calling recluses to office, restoring abolished posts, releasing long-blocked rewards, dining frugally to value grain, easing monopolies, opening mountains and marshes and simplifying passes—the realm already looks up to your Way.

sentences.zh: 今復開不諱之塗，獎直辭之路，四海希風，普天幸甚。

translations.literal: Now you again open the road of no taboo and reward the path of straight speech; the four seas hope for your wind—how fortunate all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Now you open the road of no taboo and reward straight speech; the four seas lean toward your example—what fortune for the realm!

sentences.zh: 舉蒙採問，敢不悉心，謹條鄙見，置陳如左。

translations.literal: Having been included in this inquiry, I dare not withhold my utmost; I respectfully set forth my humble views and place them before you as follows.
translations.idiomatic: Called to answer, I dare not hold back; I respectfully lay out my humble views below.

sentences.zh: 辭理違謬，伏用震讋。

translations.literal: If my wording errs, I prostrate myself in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Should my words miss the mark, I tremble to receive your correction.

sentences.zh: 夫用兵之道，自古所慎。

translations.literal: The way of employing troops has from antiquity been treated with caution.
translations.idiomatic: The art of war has always been approached with caution.

sentences.zh: 頃干戈未戢，戰備宜修，而卒不素練，兵非夙習。

translations.literal: Recently arms have not yet been laid down and war preparations ought to be improved, yet the soldiers are not trained in peacetime and the troops are not practiced over long years.
translations.idiomatic: Arms are not yet stilled and preparations should be sharpened, yet the ranks are untrained and the men unseasoned.

sentences.zh: 且戎衛之職，多非其才，或以資厚素加，或以祿薄帶帖，或寵由權門，恩自私假，既無將領，虛尸榮祿。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the duties of frontier guard many are not fit for the post: some are promoted for old wealth, some hold nominal posts for thin salary, some are favored through powerful families, some owe favor to private connections—they have no commanders yet occupy honorary salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Many frontier posts go to the unfit: some buy rank with wealth, some hold empty titles for thin pay, some enter through powerful patrons—without real commanders they still draw honorable stipends.

sentences.zh: 至於邊城舉燧，羽驛交馳，而望其擐甲推鋒，立功閫外，譬緣木求魚，不可得矣。

translations.literal: When border beacons are raised and urgent dispatches fly, yet we expect them to don armor and press the van to win merit outside the pass—it is like climbing a tree to catch fish; it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: When beacons blaze and couriers race, to expect such men to arm, lead the charge, and win glory beyond the passes is to fish in a tree—it cannot happen.

sentences.zh: 常謂臨難命師，皆出倉卒，驅烏合之眾，隸造次之主，貌疏情乖，有若胡、越，豈能使其同力，拔危濟難！

translations.literal: I have often thought that when troops are ordered in peril it is always in haste: driving a mob gathered on the spot, under commanders appointed overnight, their faces strangers and their hearts at odds like Hu and Yue—how could they unite their strength and rescue danger!
translations.idiomatic: Troops sent into crisis are always mustered in haste: a mob under overnight commanders, strangers to one another in heart as Hu and Yue are—how can they unite to save the state?

sentences.zh: 故奔北相望，覆敗繼有。

translations.literal: Hence routs face one another and defeats follow in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hence rout follows rout and defeat piles on defeat.

sentences.zh: 今欲改選將校，皆得其人，分臺見將，各以配給，領、護二軍，為其揔統。

translations.literal: Now I wish to reform the selection of commanders so that each post has the right man, assign the generals now at court each his complement, and have the two armies of the Palace and Protector as their overall command.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to choose commanders who truly fit their posts, assign each general at court his proper complement, and place the Palace and Protector armies over them as supreme command.

sentences.zh: 令撫養士卒，使恩信先加，農隙校獵，以習其事，三令五申，以齊其心，使動止應規，進退中律，然後畜銳觀釁，因時而動，摧敵陷堅，折衝於外。

translations.literal: Let them nurture the soldiers so that favor and trust come first; drill them in the hunting intervals between farming seasons; repeat orders again and again to align their hearts; make movement and rest answer to rule and advance and retreat keep to measure—then store sharpness, watch for the moment, move when the time comes, break the enemy and pierce the hard, and repulse the foe abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Train the men with kindness first; drill them between harvests; repeat orders until their hearts are one; make every movement lawful—then hoard strength, watch the moment, strike when time serves, and break the enemy abroad.

sentences.zh: 孫子曰：「視卒如赤子，故可與之共死。」

translations.literal: Sunzi said: 'Treat the soldiers as infants and they will go to death with you.'
translations.idiomatic: Sunzi said: 'Regard the soldiers as your infants, and they will die with you.'

sentences.zh: 所以張弮效爭先之心，吮癰致必盡之命，豈不由恩著者士輕其生，令明者卒畢其力。

translations.literal: Hence they draw the bow and vie to be first, suck the abscess and give their utmost life—is it not because where grace is shown men lightly hold their lives, and where orders are clear soldiers exhaust their strength?
translations.idiomatic: So men string the bow and race to be first, suck the boil and give their last breath—when grace is deep they lightly risk life; when orders are clear they spend their strength to the end.

sentences.zh: 考心跡事，如或有在，妄陳膚知，追懼乖謬。

translations.literal: Considering heart and deed, if anything here holds, I rashly state my shallow knowledge and fear afterward that it errs.
translations.idiomatic: If any of this accords with your intent, I offer it despite my shallowness and fear I may miss the mark.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書令，加散騎常侍，將軍如故；

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing and given Regular Attendant, his generalship unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Regular Attendant, his generalship unchanged;

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部，尋進號衛將軍，中書監、尚書令如故。

translations.literal: granted one set of martial pipes and drums; soon he was advanced to General Who Guards the Realm, his directorship of the Secretariat and of the Masters of Writing unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: he received martial pipes and drums, and soon was advanced to General Who Guards the Realm while keeping his secretariat and directorship.

sentences.zh: 宏少而多病，大明二年疾動，求解尚書令，以本號開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，中書監如故。

translations.literal: Hong had been ill from youth; in the second year of Daming his illness worsened and he asked to be relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing, taking his original title with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, plus Regular Attendant, his directorship of the Secretariat unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Sickly from youth, in the second year of Daming his illness worsened; he asked to leave the directorship, keeping his old title with Three Excellencies privilege and Regular Attendant, still Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未拜，其年薨，時年二十五。

translations.literal: Before he could receive appointment he died that year, aged twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment was conferred he died that year, aged twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、司徒，中書監如故，給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Regular Attendant and Minister of Works, his directorship of the Secretariat unchanged, and twenty halberd-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received Regular Attendant and Minister of Works, kept his secretariat, and was granted twenty halberd-bearers.

sentences.zh: 上痛悼甚至，每朔望輒出臨靈，自為墓誌銘并序。

translations.literal: The Emperor grieved exceedingly; on each new and full moon he went out to mourn at the bier and himself composed the epitaph and preface.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned deeply; on every new and full moon he went to the bier, and wrote the epitaph and preface himself.

sentences.zh: 與東揚州刺史顏竣詔曰：「宏夙情業尚，素心令績，雖年未及壯，願言兼申。

translations.literal: In an edict to Yan Jun, Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, he said: 'Hong's innate bent and conduct, his pure heart and fine achievement—though his years had not reached full manhood, his aspirations were already fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: He told Yan Jun, inspector of Eastern Yangzhou: 'Hong's native bent and pure heart, his fine promise—though not yet fully grown, his will was already whole.

sentences.zh: 謂天道可倚，輔仁無妄，雖寢患淹時，慮不至禍。

translations.literal: I thought Heaven's way could be relied on and that virtue aiding the good would not fail; though his illness lingered, I did not expect disaster.
translations.idiomatic: I trusted Heaven's way and believed kindness would be repaid; though illness lingered, I never thought calamity would come.

sentences.zh: 豈圖祐善虛設，一旦永謝，驚惋摧慟，五內交殞。

translations.literal: Who could have known that favoring the good was empty, that in a single morning he was gone forever! Shock, grief, and anguish rend my inmost parts.
translations.idiomatic: Who knew Heaven's favor was hollow—that in one morning he was gone forever! Grief and shock shatter me within.

sentences.zh: 平生未遠，舉目如昨，而賞對遊娛，緬同千載，哀酷纏綿，實增痛切。

translations.literal: His life was not long past, and to look up was as yesterday; yet rewards and companionship in pleasure seem a thousand years away—grief cruel and lingering truly deepens the pain.
translations.idiomatic: His death is still so near that it feels like yesterday, yet shared joys now lie a thousand years away; cruel grief clings on and cuts deeper still.

sentences.zh: 卿情均休戚，重以周旋，乖坼少時，奄成今古，聞問傷惋，當何可言。」

translations.literal: Your feelings share my joy and sorrow, and our long association besides; parted after so brief a time, suddenly become past and present—hearing of it wounds and grieves; what can be said?
translations.idiomatic: You shared my joys and sorrows, and our long friendship besides; after so brief a separation he has suddenly become one of the ancients. Hearing the news wounds and grieves me; what can be said?"

sentences.zh: 五年，益諸弟國各千戶，先薨者不在其例，唯宏追益。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the fiefs of all the younger brothers were increased by one thousand households each; those who had died earlier were not included—only Hong received a posthumous increase.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 every living prince's fief gained a thousand households; those already dead were excluded—only Hong was increased posthumously.

sentences.zh: 子景素，少愛文義，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Jingsu from youth loved literary meaning and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingsu loved literature from youth and bore his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，為寧朔將軍、南濟陰太守，徙歷陽、南譙二郡太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Southern Jiyin, then transferred to be Administrator of Liyang and Southern Qiao, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming he became General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Southern Jiyin, then of Liyang and Southern Qiao.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎，不拜。

translations.literal: Gentleman Attendant of the Masters of Writing—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered Gentleman Attendant of the Masters of Writing and declined.

sentences.zh: 監南豫、豫二州諸軍事、輔國將軍、南豫州刺史，又不拜。

translations.literal: Commander of military affairs in the two provinces of Southern Yu and Yu, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou—again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was named to command Southern Yu and Yu, as General Who Assists the State and inspector of Southern Yuzhou, and again declined.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，太子中庶子，領步兵校尉，太子左衛率，加給事中，冠軍將軍、南兗州刺史，丹陽尹，吳興太守，使持節、監湘州諸軍事、湘州刺史，將軍並如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong's reign he was Crown Prince Household Aide, Colonel of Footsoldiers, Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard, plus Supervisor in the Imperial Secretariat, General Who Crowns the Army and Inspector of Southern Yan, Governor of Danyang, Administrator of Wuxing, Bearer of the Staff and Commander of military affairs in Xiangzhou and Inspector of Xiangzhou—all his generalships unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he served the crown prince, then as General Who Crowns the Army, inspector of Southern Yan, governor of Danyang, administrator of Wuxing, and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 進號左將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，都督荊、湘、雍、益、梁、寧、南、北秦八州諸軍事、左將軍、荊州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi he was made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in the eight provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the Left and Inspector of Jingzhou, his Bearer of the Staff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi he commanded eight provinces as General of the Left and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵為散騎常侍、後將軍、太常，未拜。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Regular Attendant, General of the Rear Army, and Minister of Ceremonies—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Regular Attendant, General of the Rear Army, and Minister of Ceremonies, and declined.

sentences.zh: 授使持節、都督南徐、南兗、兗、徐、青、冀六州諸軍事、鎮軍將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of six provinces, General Who Guards the Army, and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received Bearer of the Staff, command of six provinces, General Who Guards the Army, and the inspectorship of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範為逆，景素雖纂集兵眾，以赴朝廷為名，而陰懷兩端。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Jingsu though he gathered troops took the court's side in name while secretly keeping two minds.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Jingsu raised troops in the court's name but hedged his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及事平，進號鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was advanced to General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he was made General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 齊王為南兗州，景素解都督。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi held Southern Yan, Jingsu was relieved of overall command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qi took Southern Yan, Jingsu lost his command.

sentences.zh: 時太祖諸子盡殂，眾孫唯景素為長，建安王休祐諸子並廢徙，無在朝者。

translations.literal: At that time all the Grand Ancestor's sons had died; among the grandsons only Jingsu was eldest, and the sons of Prince Xiuren of Jian'an had all been deposed and banished—none remained at court.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Grand Ancestor's sons were all dead; Jingsu was the eldest grandson, and Prince Xiuren's sons had been removed from court.

sentences.zh: 景素好文章書籍，招集才義之士，傾身禮接，以收名譽。

translations.literal: Jingsu loved literature and books, gathered men of talent and principle, bowed his person to receive them, and thereby won reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu loved books, gathered talented men, and treated them with full courtesy to win renown.

sentences.zh: 由是朝野翕然，莫不屬意焉。

translations.literal: Hence court and countryside alike turned their hopes to him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike began to look to him.

sentences.zh: 而後廢帝狂凶失道，內外皆謂景素宜當神器，唯廢帝所生陳氏親戚疾忌之。

translations.literal: The Later Deposed Emperor was wildly cruel and lost the Way; inside and outside all thought Jingsu should receive the sacred vessel—only the Chen clan, kin of the Deposed Emperor, hated and feared this.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Deposed Emperor's cruelty made many think Jingsu should take the throne—only the Chen kin of the emperor feared it.

sentences.zh: 而楊運長、阮佃夫竝太宗舊隸，貪幼少以久其權，慮景素立，不見容於長主，深相忌憚。

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang and Ruan Tianfu were both old followers of Taizong; greedy to hold power over a young ruler, they feared that if Jingsu were established they would not be tolerated by the grown sovereign and deeply dreaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang and Ruan Tianfu, Taizong's old retainers, clung to power over a child emperor and dreaded a grown Jingsu on the throne.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年，景素防閣將軍王季符失景素旨，怨恨，因單騎奔京邑，告運長、佃夫云「景素欲反」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui, Wang Jifu, a garrison officer of Jingsu, lost his favor and bore resentment; he rode alone to the capital and told Yunchang and Tianfu that 'Jingsu intends to rebel.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 3, Jingsu's officer Wang Jifu, resentful after falling from favor, rode alone to the capital and told Yunchang and Tianfu: "Jingsu intends to rebel."

sentences.zh: 運長等便欲遣軍討之，齊王及衛將軍袁粲以下並保持之，謂為不然也。

translations.literal: Yunchang and the others wished at once to send troops against him; the Prince of Qi, General Who Guards the Realm Yuan Can, and others restrained them, saying it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted troops sent at once; the Prince of Qi, Yuan Can, and others held them back.

sentences.zh: 景素亦馳遣世子延齡還都，具自申理。

translations.literal: Jingsu also hurried his heir Yanling back to the capital to state his case in full.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu sent his heir Yanling to the capital to plead his innocence.

sentences.zh: 運長等乃徙季符於梁州，又奪景素征北將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Yunchang and the others then transferred Jifu to Liangzhou and stripped Jingsu of General Who Guards the North and the privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: They banished Jifu to Liangzhou and stripped Jingsu of General Who Guards the North and Three Excellencies privilege.

sentences.zh: 自是廢帝狂悖日甚，朝野並屬心景素，陳氏及運長等彌相猜疑。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Deposed Emperor grew more frenzied daily; court and countryside both set their hearts on Jingsu, and the Chen clan and Yunchang grew more suspicious of each other.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew wilder; hopes fixed on Jingsu, and suspicion between the Chens and Yunchang deepened.

sentences.zh: 景素因此稍為自防之計，與司馬廬江何季穆、錄事參軍陳郡殷濔、記室參軍濟陽蔡履、中兵參軍略陽垣慶延、左右賀文超等謀之。

translations.literal: Jingsu therefore gradually made plans of self-defense with his Army Aide He Jimu of Lujiang, Recorder Yin Mi of Chen, Secretary Cai Lü of Jiyang, Army Aide Yuan Qingyan of Lueyang, and his attendant He Wenchao.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu began to plan with He Jimu, Yin Mi, Cai Lü, Yuan Qingyan, and He Wenchao.

sentences.zh: 以參軍沈顒、毋丘文子、左暄、州西曹王潭等為爪牙。

translations.literal: He made the aides Shen Yong, Wuqiu Wenzi, Zuo Xuan, and Wang Tan of the western bureau his claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yong, Wuqiu Wenzi, Zuo Xuan, and Wang Tan became his agents.

sentences.zh: 季穆薦從弟豫之為參軍。

translations.literal: Jimu recommended his cousin Yu Zhi as Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Jimu recommended his cousin Yu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 景素遣豫之、潭、文超等去來京邑，多與金帛，要結才力之士。

translations.literal: Jingsu sent Yu Zhi, Tan, Wenchao, and others back and forth to the capital, giving much gold and silk to win men of force and talent.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yu Zhi, Tan, and Wenchao to the capital with gold and silk to recruit strong men.

sentences.zh: 由是冠軍將軍黃回、游擊將軍高道慶、輔國將軍曹欣之、前軍韓道清、長水校尉郭蘭之、羽林監垣祗祖，並皆響附，其餘武人失職不得志者，莫不歸之。

translations.literal: Hence General Who Crowns the Army Huang Hui, General Who Strikes the Enemy Gao Daoqing, General Who Assists the State Cao Xinzi, Vanguard Han Daoqing, Colonel of the Long River Guo Lanzhi, and Colonel of the Feathered Forest Yuan Qizu all responded; other martial men out of office and ambition likewise joined.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui, Gao Daoqing, Cao Xinzi, Han Daoqing, Guo Lanzhi, and Yuan Qizu all rallied to him, with every discontented soldier besides.

sentences.zh: 時廢帝單馬獨出，遊走郊野，曹欣之謀據石頭，韓道清、郭蘭之欲說齊王使同，若不回者圖之。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor rode out alone to roam the suburbs; Cao Xinzi plotted to seize Shitou, Han Daoqing and Guo Lanzhi wished to win the Prince of Qi to join them, and if he refused, to deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode out alone; Cao Xinzi planned to seize Shitou while Han and Guo tried to win or remove the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 候廢帝出行，因眾作難，事克奉景素。

translations.literal: They would wait for the Deposed Emperor to go out and then raise trouble among the masses; when successful they would install Jingsu.
translations.idiomatic: They would strike when the emperor went abroad and set Jingsu on the throne.

sentences.zh: 景素每禁駐之，未欲匆匆舉動。

translations.literal: Jingsu always restrained them and did not wish to act in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu always held them back from rash action.

sentences.zh: 運長密遣傖人周天賜偽投景素，勸為異計；

translations.literal: Yunchang secretly sent the bondservant Zhou Tianci to pretend to defect to Jingsu and urge a separate plot;
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang sent Zhou Tianci to feign defection and urge rebellion;

sentences.zh: 景素知為運長所遣，即斬之，遣司馬孫謙送首還台。

translations.literal: Jingsu knew he was sent by Yunchang, beheaded him at once, and sent Army Aide Sun Qian to deliver the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu knew the trap, executed Tianci, and sent Sun Qian with his head to court.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年七月，垣祗祖率數百人奔景素，云京邑已潰亂，勸令速入。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Yuanhui, Yuan Qizu led several hundred men to Jingsu, saying the capital was already in chaos and urging him to enter quickly.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 4, month 7, Yuan Qizu fled to Jingsu with hundreds of men, claiming the capital had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 景素信之，即便舉兵，負戈至者數千人。

translations.literal: Jingsu believed it and immediately raised troops; those who came bearing arms numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Believing him, Jingsu rose at once; several thousand armed men gathered.

sentences.zh: 運長/等常疑景素有異志，及聞祗祖叛走，便纂嚴備辦。

translations.literal: Yunchang and the others had long suspected Jingsu of disloyalty; hearing of Qizu's defection, they mustered arms and made ready.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Qizu, Yunchang and the others mobilized.

sentences.zh: 齊王出屯玄武湖，冠軍將軍任農夫、黃回、左軍將軍李安民各領步軍，右軍將軍張保率水軍，竝北討。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi encamped at Xuanwu Lake; General Who Crowns the Army Ren Nongfu, Huang Hui, and General of the Left Army Li Anmin each led infantry; General of the Right Army Zhang Bao led the navy—all marched north to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi camped at Xuanwu Lake; Ren Nongfu, Huang Hui, and Li Anmin led foot; Zhang Bao led ships north against Jingsu.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、南豫州刺史段佛榮為都統，其餘眾軍相繼進。

translations.literal: General Who Crowns the Army and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou Duan Furong was overall commander; the rest of the armies followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Furong of Southern Yuzhou commanded; other armies followed.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍齊王世子鎮東府城。

translations.literal: The heir of General Who Crowns the Army, the Prince of Qi, garrisoned the Eastern Palace city.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi's heir held the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 齊王知黃回有異圖，故使安民、佛榮俱行以防之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi knew Huang Hui harbored other designs and therefore sent Anmin and Furong together to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Huang Hui's treachery, the Prince of Qi paired Anmin with Furong to watch him.

sentences.zh: 景素欲斷據竹里，以拒臺軍。

translations.literal: Jingsu wished to hold Zhuli and block the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu meant to hold Zhuli against the court army.

sentences.zh: 垣慶延、祗祖、沈顒等曰：「今天時旱熱，臺軍遠來疲困，引之使至，以逸待勞，可一戰而克也。」

translations.literal: Yuan Qingyan, Qizu, Shen Yong, and others said: 'Today the season is hot and dry; the imperial army comes far and is weary—draw them on until they arrive, meet them rested, and one battle will conquer.'
translations.idiomatic: Qingyan and others urged: 'The heat will exhaust the distant court army—let them come, then strike fresh and win at once.'

sentences.zh: 殷濔等固爭不能。

translations.literal: Yin Mi and others argued hard but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Mi argued in vain.

sentences.zh: 農夫等既至，放火燒市邑，而垣慶延等各相顧望，竝無鬥志。

translations.literal: When Nongfu and the others arrived they set fire to the market towns, while Yuan Qingyan and the rest only looked at one another, all without fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The court army burned the towns; Jingsu's officers lost heart.

sentences.zh: 景素本乏威略，恇擾不知所為。

translations.literal: Jingsu by nature lacked authority and strategy; panicked, he did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu lacked command; in panic he froze.

sentences.zh: 時張保水軍泊西渚，景素左右勇士數十人，竝荊楚快手，自相要結，擊水軍，應時摧陷，斬張保，而諸將不相應赴，復為臺軍所破。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Bao's navy was moored at West Ford; several dozen of Jingsu's champions, all expert fighters of Jing and Chu, banded together, struck the navy, destroyed it at once, and killed Zhang Bao—but the other generals did not support them and they were broken again by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu's champions smashed Zhang Bao's fleet, but without support were beaten again.

sentences.zh: 臺軍既薄城池，顒先眾叛走，垣祗祖次之，其餘諸軍相係奔敗。

translations.literal: When the imperial army pressed the walls, Yong was first to flee at the head of the troops; Qizu followed; the rest fled in chains.
translations.idiomatic: As the court army closed in, Yong fled first, then Qizu, then all the rest.

sentences.zh: 左暄驍果有膽力，欲為景素盡節，而所配兵力甚弱，猶力戰不退，於萬歲樓下橫射臺軍，不能禁，然後退散。

translations.literal: Zuo Xuan was brave and resolute and wished to die for Jingsu, but his allotted troops were very few; still he fought hard without retreating, shooting the imperial army from beneath the Wansui Tower until he could not hold them and only then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Xuan fought to the last beneath Wansui Tower before he broke.

sentences.zh: 右衛殿中將軍張倪奴、前軍將軍周盤龍攻陷京城，倪奴禽景素斬之，時年二十五，即葬京口。

translations.literal: Palace Guard Commander of the Right Army Zhang Ninu and Vanguard General Zhou Panlong stormed the capital; Ninu seized Jingsu and beheaded him. He was twenty-five and was buried at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ninu and Zhou Panlong took the city; Ninu seized and beheaded Jingsu, aged twenty-five, buried at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 垣慶延、祗祖、左暄、賀文超竝伏誅；

translations.literal: Yuan Qingyan, Qizu, Zuo Xuan, and He Wenchao were all executed;
translations.idiomatic: Qingyan, Qizu, Xuan, and Wenchao were executed;

sentences.zh: 殷濔、蔡履徙梁州；

translations.literal: Yin Mi and Cai Lü were banished to Liangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Mi and Cai Lü were exiled to Liangzhou;

sentences.zh: 何季穆先遷官，故不及禍；

translations.literal: He Jimu had earlier been transferred and therefore escaped punishment;
translations.idiomatic: He Jimu had been transferred and escaped;

sentences.zh: 其餘皆逃亡，值赦得免。

translations.literal: the rest fled and were pardoned at the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: the rest fled and were spared at the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 景素既敗，曹欣之反告韓道清、郭蘭之之謀，道清等竝誅。

translations.literal: After Jingsu's defeat, Cao Xinzi reported the plot of Han Daoqing and Guo Lanzhi, and Daoqing and the others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xinzi then denounced Han and Guo; they were executed.

sentences.zh: 黃回、高道慶等，齊王撫之如舊。

translations.literal: Huang Hui, Gao Daoqing, and the others the Prince of Qi treated as before.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui and Gao Daoqing the Prince of Qi kept in favor.

sentences.zh: 景素子延齡及二少子，竝從誅。

translations.literal: Jingsu's son Yanling and two younger sons were all executed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu's heir Yanling and two younger sons were killed.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，封長沙成王義欣子勰第三子恬為秭歸縣侯，食邑千戶，繼宏後。

translations.literal: That winter the third son of Prince Cheng of Changsha Yixin, Tian, was enfeoffed Marquis of Zigui with a fief of one thousand households to succeed Hong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Tian, third son of Prince Cheng of Changsha, succeeded Hong as Marquis of Zigui.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明二年，卒，國除。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming of Emperor Shun he died and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shun's Shengming 2 he died and the fief ended.

sentences.zh: 張倪奴以禽景素功，封筑陽縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Zhang Ninu for seizing Jingsu was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhuyang with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ninu was made Marquis of Zhuyang for capturing Jingsu.

sentences.zh: 景素敗後，故記室參軍王螭、故主簿何昌宇竝上書訟景素之冤。

translations.literal: After Jingsu's defeat, the former Secretary Wang Chi and former Registrar He Changyu both submitted memorials pleading Jingsu's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chi and He Changyu later memorialized for Jingsu's innocence.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，建元初，故景素秀才劉璡又上書曰：

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, in the first year of Jianyuan the former licentiate of Jingsu, Liu Zan, again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took power, Liu Zan, Jingsu's former licentiate, memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 臣聞曾子孝於其親而沈乎水，介生忠於其主而焚於火，何則？

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Zengzi was filial toward his parents yet sank in water, and Jiesheng was loyal to his lord yet burned in fire—why?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Zengzi, filial to his parents, drowned, and Jiesheng, loyal to his lord, burned—why?

sentences.zh: 仁也不必可依，信也不必可恃。

translations.literal: Benevolence cannot always be relied on, nor faith always be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue cannot always protect you; trust cannot always save you.

sentences.zh: 昔者墨翟議雲梯於荊臺之下，宋人逐之；

translations.literal: Formerly Mozi argued against cloud-ladders below the Jing Terrace and the Song people drove him out;
translations.idiomatic: Mozi argued against siege engines at the Jing Terrace and Song drove him out;

sentences.zh: 夷叔為衛軍隱難於晉，公子殪之；

translations.literal: Boyi and Shuqi hid with the Wei army in difficulty in Jin, and the lord's son killed them;
translations.idiomatic: Boyi and Shuqi hid with a Jin army in distress and were killed;

sentences.zh: 李牧北逝強胡之旗，南拒全秦之卒；

translations.literal: Li Mu fled north before the banners of the strong Hu and south blocked the whole army of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu turned back the Hu and held off all Qin;

sentences.zh: 趙王不圖其功，賜以利劍；

translations.literal: the King of Zhao did not consider his merit and rewarded him with a sharp sword;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's king ignored his merit and gave him a sword instead;

sentences.zh: 陳蕃白首固義，忘生事主；

translations.literal: Chen Fan white-haired held to righteousness and forgot life serving his lord;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan, white-haired, died serving his lord;

sentences.zh: 漢靈不明其忠，卒被刑戮。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling of Han did not see his loyalty and he was finally punished by execution.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling did not see it and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 彼數子者，皆身棲青雲之上，而困於泥塵之裏，誠以危行不容於衰世，孤立聚尤於眾人，加讒諂蛆蠱其中，謗隙蜂飛而至故也。

translations.literal: Those several men all lodged their bodies above the blue clouds yet were trapped in the mud of dust—truly because perilous conduct cannot be tolerated in a declining age, standing alone gathers blame from the multitude, with slander and flattery breeding within and calumny flying like bees.
translations.idiomatic: They stood high yet were trapped in mud—loyalty in a bad age draws slander like bees.

sentences.zh: 臣聞浸潤之行，骨肉離絕，疑似一至，君臣易心，此中山所以歔欷奏樂，孟博所以慷慨囊頭者也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that creeping slander separates flesh and bone, and once suspicion arises lord and minister change heart—this is why the Prince of Zhongshan sighed and played music, and why Meng Bo wrapped his head in a bag.
translations.idiomatic: Slander separates kin and turns lords against ministers—as with Zhongshan and Meng Bo.

sentences.zh: 臣每惟故舉將宋建平王之禍，悲徹骨髓，氣凝霜霰。

translations.literal: Your servant often thinks of the disaster of the former Prince of Pingping and grief pierces marrow, breath congealing like frost.
translations.idiomatic: I think of Prince Hong's fate and grief pierces my bones.

sentences.zh: 今璿鼎啟運，人神改物，生罪尚宥，死冤必申。

translations.literal: Now the sacred tripod has begun its turn, men and spirits have changed; living guilt is still pardoned—dead wrong must be redressed.
translations.idiomatic: Now a new age begins; the living are pardoned—the dead must be cleared.

sentences.zh: 臣誠不忍王之負謗而不雪，故敢明言其理。

translations.literal: Your servant truly cannot bear that the Prince bears slander uncleared and therefore dares to state the principle plainly.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear the Prince's name to lie under slander and state his case.

sentences.zh: 臣聞孝悌為志者，不以犯上，曾子不逆薪而爨，知其不為暴也；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that those whose aim is filial piety do not offend their superiors; Zengzi did not move firewood to cook, knowing he would not be violent;
translations.idiomatic: Filial sons do not rebel—Zengzi would not cook with stolen fuel;

sentences.zh: 秦仁獲麑，知其可為傅也。

translations.literal: Qin Ren captured a fawn and knew he could be a tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ren spared a fawn and knew he could teach.

sentences.zh: 臣聞王之事獻太妃也，朝夕不違養，甘苦不見色。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in serving the late Imperial Consort the Prince from morning to evening did not neglect nurture, and in bitter or sweet never changed countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince served the late Consort without failing day or night.

sentences.zh: 帳下進珍饌，太妃未食，王投箸輟飯。

translations.literal: When the attendants brought delicacies, if the Consort had not eaten the Prince cast down his chopsticks and stopped eating.
translations.idiomatic: If she had not eaten, he would not eat.

sentences.zh: 太妃起居有不安，王傍行蓬髮。

translations.literal: When the Consort's daily routine was unsettled, the Prince walked beside her with hair unbound.
translations.idiomatic: When she was ill he walked disheveled at her side.

sentences.zh: 臣聞求忠臣者於孝子之門，安有孝如王而不忠者乎？

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that one seeks loyal ministers at the door of filial sons—how could there be filial piety like the Prince's yet disloyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers come from filial sons—how could he be disloyal?

sentences.zh: 其可明一也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the first point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first proof.

sentences.zh: 當泰始、元徽中，王公貴人無謁景寧陵者，王獨抗情而行，不以趨時捨義，出鎮入朝，必俛拜陵所。

translations.literal: In the Taishi and Yuanhui eras the nobles did not visit Jingning Mausoleum; the Prince alone went with upright feeling, not discarding righteousness to suit the times; going out to a post or entering court he always bowed at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When others abandoned the imperial tombs, he alone still bowed there.

sentences.zh: 王尚不棄先君，豈背今君乎？

translations.literal: The Prince did not abandon the former lord—would he betray the present lord?
translations.idiomatic: He honored the dead—would he betray the living?

sentences.zh: 其可明二也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the second point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second proof.

sentences.zh: 王博聞而容眾，與諫而愛士，與人言呴呴若有傷。

translations.literal: The Prince was broad in learning and tolerant of the multitude, received remonstrance and loved scholars; in speaking with others he was gentle as if pained.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed counsel and loved scholars, speaking gently to all.

sentences.zh: 聞人之善，譽而進之；

translations.literal: Hearing of others' good he praised and advanced them;
translations.idiomatic: He praised good and advanced it;

sentences.zh: 見人之惡，掩而誨之。

translations.literal: seeing others' evil he covered and admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: he hid faults and taught better.

sentences.zh: 李蔚之，蓬廬之寒素也，王枉駕而訊之；

translations.literal: Li Weizhi was a poor scholar of a thatched hut; the Prince bent his carriage to inquire of him;
translations.idiomatic: He sought out the poor scholar Li Weizhi;

sentences.zh: 何季穆等，宣簡王之舊也，王提挈以升之。

translations.literal: He Jimu and others were old associates of Prince Xuanjian; the Prince raised them up.
translations.idiomatic: he raised He Jimu and other old retainers of Prince Hong.

sentences.zh: 王虛己以厚天下之士，尚不欲傷一人之心，何乃親戚圖相菹膾乎？

translations.literal: The Prince emptied himself to honor the empire's scholars and would not willingly wound one heart—how could kinsmen plot mutual slaughter?
translations.idiomatic: He honored all scholars—would he slaughter kin?

sentences.zh: 其可明三也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the third point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third proof.

sentences.zh: 臣昔以法曹參軍，奉訊於聽朝之末。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly as Legal Affairs Aide attended inquiries at the end of court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: I once served in legal affairs at court's end.

sentences.zh: 王每斷獄，降聲辭，和顏色，以待士女之訟。

translations.literal: When the Prince judged cases he lowered his voice and softened his countenance to await the suits of gentlemen and ladies.
translations.idiomatic: In judging cases he spoke softly and kindly to litigants.

sentences.zh: 時見夏伯以童子縲縶，王愴然改貌，用不加刑。

translations.literal: Once he saw Xiabo, a boy in bonds, and the Prince changed countenance in grief and did not add punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing a boy prisoner, he grieved and spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 徐州嘗歲饑，王散秩粟俸帛，以斷民之乏。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou once had famine the Prince distributed his salary grain and silk to relieve the people's want.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he gave his salary grain to the people.

sentences.zh: 蠲理冤疑，咸息徭務，所在皆有愛於民。

translations.literal: He cleared doubtful wrongs and everywhere eased corvée duties; in every place he had love for the people.
translations.idiomatic: He eased taxes and won love wherever he ruled.

sentences.zh: 臣聞善人，國之紀也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that good men are the norm of a state.
translations.idiomatic: Good men are a state's standard.

sentences.zh: 安有仁於民庶，而虐其宗國者乎？

translations.literal: How could one be benevolent to the common people yet cruel to the imperial clan?
translations.idiomatic: How could he love the people yet harm the clan?

sentences.zh: 其可明四也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth proof.

sentences.zh: 王脩身潔行，言無近雜，內去聲酌之娛，外無田弋之好。

translations.literal: The Prince cultivated his person and purified his conduct; his words had no vulgar admixture; within he put away the pleasure of music and wine, without he had no love of hunting in fields.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly: no vulgar talk, no music and wine within, no hunting without.

sentences.zh: 每所臨踐，不加穿築，直衛不繁，第宅無改。

translations.literal: In every place he governed he added no digging or building; his straight guards were not numerous; his mansion was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he ruled he built nothing extra, kept few guards, and left his residence unchanged.

sentences.zh: 荊州高齋，刻楹柏構，王廢而不處。

translations.literal: In Jingzhou the high studio had carved pillars and cypress beams; the Prince abandoned it and would not dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: A carved hall stood in Jingzhou; he refused to live in it.

sentences.zh: 昔朝廷欲賜王東陵甲第，又辭而不當。

translations.literal: Formerly the court wished to grant the Prince a mansion of the first rank at Dongling, and again he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The court offered him a grand mansion at Dongling; he declined.

sentences.zh: 兩宮所遺珍玩，塵於笥篋。

translations.literal: The rare curios sent by the two palaces lay dusty in chests.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts from both palaces gathered dust in his chests.

sentences.zh: 無它嬖私，不耽內寵，姬嬙數人，皆詔令所賜。

translations.literal: He had no other favorites or private attachments, did not indulge in inner favor; the several concubines were all granted by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: He kept no private favorites; his few concubines were all imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 王身食不踰一肉，器用瓦素，時有獻鏤玉器，王顧謂何昌宇曰：「我持此安所用哉？」

translations.literal: The Prince's own food did not exceed one dish of meat; his vessels were plain tile; when carved jade vessels were offered he turned to He Changyu and said: 'What use have I for these?'
translations.idiomatic: He ate simply on plain ware; when jade was offered he asked He Changyu, 'What use are these to me?'

sentences.zh: 乃謝而反之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he declined and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: He thanked the donor and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 王恭己蹈義若此。

translations.literal: The Prince's respectful self-restraint and treading in righteousness were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his restraint and integrity.

sentences.zh: 其可明五也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fifth proof.

sentences.zh: 王之在荊州也，時獻太妃初薨，宋明帝新棄天下，京畿諸王又相繼非命，王乃徵入為太常，楚下人士並勸勿下，王謂：「為臣而距先皇之命，不忠；為子不奉親之窀穸，不孝。」

translations.literal: When the Prince was in Jingzhou, Consort Xian had just died, Emperor Ming of Song had newly abandoned the realm, and the princes in the capital region had also one after another died unnatural deaths. The Prince was then summoned in to become Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and the people below in Chu all urged him not to go down. The Prince said, "As a minister, to resist the command of the former emperor would be disloyal; as a son, not to attend to my parent's burial would be unfilial."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince was in Jingzhou, Consort Xian had just died, Emperor Ming had just passed away, and the princes around the capital had one after another met unnatural deaths. He was summoned in as Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and the people of Chu urged him not to go. The Prince said, "As a minister, to resist the late emperor's command would be disloyal; as a son, not to attend to my parent's burial would be unfilial."

sentences.zh: 於是棄西州之重，而匍伏北闕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abandoned the weighty position in the western province and crawled prostrate to the northern palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore gave up the weighty command in the western province and came humbly to the northern palace gate.

sentences.zh: 王若志欲倔強，便應高枕江漢，何為屈折而受制於人乎？

translations.literal: If the Prince had intended obstinate resistance, he should have rested high on his pillow between the Yangzi and Han; why would he bend himself and accept control by others?
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince had intended defiance, he could have rested securely between the Yangzi and Han. Why would he have bent himself and submitted to others?

sentences.zh: 其可明六也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the sixth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the sixth proof.

sentences.zh: 王名高海內，義重太山，耆幼懷仁，士庶慕德。

translations.literal: The Prince's fame was high within the seas, his righteousness heavy as Mount Tai; old and young cherished benevolence, gentlemen and commoners admired virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His fame filled the realm, his virtue weighed like Tai; young and old honored him.

sentences.zh: 故從昏者忌明，同枉者毀正，搦弦為鉤，張一作百，行坐欬嚏，皆生風塵。

translations.literal: Hence those who follow darkness hate brightness, those who share perversity destroy the upright; twisting a string into a hook, making one into a hundred—sitting, walking, coughing, or sneezing all raise dust.
translations.idiomatic: The corrupt hate the upright; slanderers twist one word into a hundred crimes.

sentences.zh: 會王季符負罪流謗，事會讒人之心，權醜相扇，鴟梟奮翼。

translations.literal: When Wang Jifu, guilty and spreading slander, met the slanderers' hearts, power and ugliness fanned each other and owls and kites spread their wings.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu slandered him, villains fanned the flames like birds of prey.

sentences.zh: 王雖遘愍離凶，而誠分彌款，散情中孚，揮斥滿素。

translations.literal: Though the Prince met grief and separation and disaster, his sincerity grew fuller; he scattered feeling in inner faith and cast off fullness in plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Though wronged, he remained sincere and open-hearted.

sentences.zh: 虞玩之銜使歸旋，世子入質京邑，續解徐州，請身東第，後求會稽，降階外撫。

translations.literal: Yu Wanzhi returned from mission; the heir entered the capital as hostage; he successively relinquished Xuzhou, asked to reside in the Eastern Palace, later sought Kuaiji, and lowered his rank to govern abroad.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his heir to court, gave up Xuzhou, asked for the Eastern Palace, then for Kuaiji—every step showed submission.

sentences.zh: 虞玩、殷煥實為詮譯，誠心殷勤，備留聖聽。

translations.literal: Yu Wan and Yin Huan truly interpreted for him, with sincere and earnest hearts, fully leaving word for the sacred ear.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wan and Yin Huan pleaded his case earnestly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 王若侜張跋扈，何事若斯？

translations.literal: If the Prince were arrogant and overbearing, why would he have done such things?
translations.idiomatic: If he were rebellious, why act like this?

sentences.zh: 其可明七也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the seventh point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the seventh proof.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，日同殊論，蒼梧之衰德既彰，群小之姦慝彌廣，下盈其毒，上不可依。

translations.literal: From then on each day brought different opinions; the Deposed Emperor's decayed virtue was already manifest, the petty men's wickedness grew wider, below brimmed with poison and above could not be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: After that the emperor's evil showed; courtiers poisoned the realm and the throne could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 時長王並見誅鋤，公卿如蹈虎尾，眾人翕翕，莫不住仰於王。

translations.literal: At that time the elder princes were all executed; the high officials were as if treading a tiger's tail; the multitude in unison all looked up to the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were slaughtered; officials trembled; all eyes turned to the Prince.

sentences.zh: 廂閤諸人，同謀異志，王心不從利，忠不背本，執周天賜而斬之，以距王宜與等，遣司馬孫謙歸款朝廷。

translations.literal: The men of the side chambers shared one plot but different aims; the Prince's heart did not follow profit, his loyalty did not betray the root—he seized Zhou Tianci and beheaded him to repulse Wang Yiyu and the others and sent Army Aide Sun Qian to declare loyalty to the court.
translations.idiomatic: His staff plotted rebellion; he executed Tianci and sent Sun Qian to swear loyalty to court.

sentences.zh: 王若欲擬非覬，寧當如此乎？

translations.literal: If the Prince wished to aim at usurpation, would he have acted thus?
translations.idiomatic: If he sought the throne, would he have done this?

sentences.zh: 其可明八也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the eighth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the eighth proof.

sentences.zh: 又是年五月以後，道路皆謂阮佃夫等欲潛圖宮禁，因兵北襲，而黃回、高道慶等傳構其事，武人獎亂，更相恐脅。

translations.literal: Again, after the fifth month of that year the roads all said Ruan Tianfu and others wished secretly to plot against the palace precincts and strike north with troops, while Huang Hui, Gao Daoqing, and others spread and framed the affair, martial men encouraging disorder and threatening one another.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifth month rumor said Ruan Tianfu would strike the palace; Huang Hui and others inflamed the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 至六月而京師徵賦車徒，將講眾北壘，都鄙疑駭，僉言釁作。

translations.literal: By the sixth month the capital levied carts and men to muster troops for northern fortifications; capital and countryside were alarmed, all saying revolt was rising.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the capital mobilized for war; everyone feared rebellion.

sentences.zh: 垣祗祖因民情囂蕩，揚聲北奔，紿辭惑眾，窮亂極禍。

translations.literal: Yuan Qizu, because the people's feelings were turbulent, raised the cry of fleeing north, deceived with words and confused the masses—extreme chaos, utmost disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Qizu exploited panic, crying that flight north was needed, and misled the crowd.

sentences.zh: 會州人自都還，說：「掖門已閉，殊不知臺中安不？」

translations.literal: When men from the province returned from the capital they said: 'The side gates are closed—we do not know whether the court is safe or not.'
translations.idiomatic: Men from the capital reported: 'The gates are shut—is the court safe?'

sentences.zh: 王既素籍異論，謂為信然，收率疲弱，志在投散，冰炭在懷，但恐遲後。

translations.literal: The Prince had long heard strange talk and believed it true; he gathered the weak and weary, his aim to scatter and flee—ice and charcoal in his breast, only fearing to be late.
translations.idiomatic: He believed the rumors, gathered weak troops, and only wanted to escape.

sentences.zh: 何圖兵以順出，翻為逆動乎？

translations.literal: Who would have thought troops sent out in loyalty would be turned into a rebellious movement?
translations.idiomatic: How could loyal mustering become rebellion?

sentences.zh: 夫往來之人，喧嘩幻惑，皆出輦轂，非從徐州起也。

translations.literal: The coming and going of men, noisy and deluding, all issued from the capital—it did not begin from Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The panic came from the capital, not from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 且臺以六月晦夜無何呼北兵已至，皆登陴抽刃，而朱方七月朔猶緩帶從容，其晚聞京都變亂，始乃鳩兵簡甲耳。

translations.literal: Moreover the court on the last night of the sixth month for no reason called northern troops already arrived—all mounted the walls and drew blades—while at Zhufang on the first of the seventh month they were still leisurely with loose belts; only that evening hearing of turmoil in the capital did they begin to gather troops and select armor.
translations.idiomatic: The court army was armed on the sixth month's last night; Jingsu only armed on the seventh after hearing of chaos.

sentences.zh: 王豈先造禍哉！

translations.literal: How could the Prince have made disaster first!
translations.idiomatic: He did not start the trouble!

sentences.zh: 其可明九也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the ninth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the ninth proof.

sentences.zh: 王聞京室有難，坐不安，食不甘，言及太后，未嘗不交巾掩泣。

translations.literal: When the Prince heard of trouble in the capital he could not sit at ease or eat with pleasure; speaking of the Empress Dowager he never failed to cover his face with his scarf and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of capital turmoil he could not eat or sit; he wept for the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 又臨危之際，撫楹而歎曰：「吾恐三才於斯絕矣。」

translations.literal: Again at the crisis he stroked the pillar and sighed: 'I fear the three powers will perish here.'
translations.idiomatic: At the crisis he sighed: 'I fear heaven, earth, and man will perish here.'

sentences.zh: 茲豈不誠在本朝，以天下為憂乎？

translations.literal: Is this not truly rooted in devotion to the dynasty and anxiety for all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Was that not love for the dynasty and the realm?
