sentences.zh: 自非深忠遠概，孰能身滅之不恤，獨眷眷國家安危哉？

translations.literal: Unless deep loyalty and far-reaching design, who could disregard his own destruction yet alone care for the state's safety?
translations.idiomatic: Only deep loyalty could make a man forget himself for the state.

sentences.zh: 其可明十也。

translations.literal: This may make clear the tenth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the tenth proof.

sentences.zh: 夫王起兵之日，止在匡救昏難，放殛姦盜，非它故也。

translations.literal: When the Prince raised troops it was only to rescue the deluded difficulty and expel wicked thieves—not for any other cause.
translations.idiomatic: He raised arms only to save the state from villains, not for himself.

sentences.zh: 請較言之。

translations.literal: I ask to compare and speak.
translations.idiomatic: Let us compare.

sentences.zh: 當時君臣之道，治亂云何？

translations.literal: At that time the way of lord and minister—was governance order or chaos?
translations.idiomatic: Was the court ordered or chaotic?

sentences.zh: 楊運長、阮佃夫為有罪邪？

translations.literal: Were Yang Yunchang and Ruan Tianfu guilty?
translations.idiomatic: Were Yang Yunchang and Ruan Tianfu guilty?

sentences.zh: 為無罪邪？

translations.literal: Or were they not guilty?
translations.idiomatic: Or innocent?

sentences.zh: 若其無罪，何故為戮？

translations.literal: If they were not guilty, why were they executed?
translations.idiomatic: If innocent, why kill them?

sentences.zh: 若其有罪，討之何辜？

translations.literal: If they were guilty, what crime in punishing them?
translations.idiomatic: If guilty, what crime in attacking them?

sentences.zh: 王豈不知君親之無將乎？

translations.literal: Did the Prince not know that none may plot against lord and parent?
translations.idiomatic: He knew one must not rebel against kin and throne.

sentences.zh: 顧以救火之家，豈遑先白丈人，非不恭也，徒以運屬陵喪，智力無所用之，蹉跌傾覆，此乃時也，豈謂反乎？

translations.literal: But in a house on fire how could one first inform the elders—it was not disrespect, only that the age was in ruin and intelligence had no use; stumbling to overturn—this was the time; how could it be called rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: In a burning house one cannot wait for permission—this was crisis, not rebellion.

sentences.zh: 果然今日王亡，明日宋亡，王何負於社稷，何媿於天下哉！

translations.literal: Truly if today the Prince dies, tomorrow Song dies—what did the Prince fail toward the altars, what shame toward all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: If he dies today, Song falls tomorrow—he owes the state nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣聞武王克商，未及下車，而封王子之墓；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when King Wu overcame Shang he had not yet descended from his chariot before enfeoffing the tomb of Prince Bi;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu enfeoffed Prince Bi's tomb before leaving his chariot;

sentences.zh: 漢高定天下，過大梁，躡燕、代，修信陵之祀，存望諸之裔；

translations.literal: when Han Gaozu settled the realm, passing Daliang he visited the tombs of Yan and Dai and repaired the sacrifices to Lord Xinling, preserving the descendants of Wang Zhu;
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu honored Lord Xinling and Wang Zhu;

sentences.zh: 晉世受命，亦追王陵之冤，而詔其孫為郎。

translations.literal: when Jin received the mandate it also pursued the wrong done to Wang Ling and made his grandson a Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Jin cleared Wang Ling's name and honored his heir.

sentences.zh: 夫比干，殷辛之罪人也；

translations.literal: Bigan was a criminal of Yin and Xin;
translations.idiomatic: Bigan was condemned by Shang;

sentences.zh: 無忌，魏之疑臣也；

translations.literal: Wuji was a suspect minister of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji was suspected in Wei;

sentences.zh: 樂毅，燕之逃將也；

translations.literal: Yue Yi was a fugitive general of Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi fled Yan;

sentences.zh: 彥雲，齊之賊而晉害也。

translations.literal: Yan Yun was a traitor of Qi whom Jin harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yun was Qi’s man whom Jin wronged.

sentences.zh: 適逢聖明之君，革運創制，昭功誠，蕩嫌怨，清議以天下之善也。

translations.literal: They happened to meet sage and enlightened rulers who changed the mandate and created institutions, making manifest merit and sincerity, clearing suspicion and resentment, and clarifying discussion with the good of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers cleared their names and honored their merit.

sentences.zh: 或殊世而相明，故四賢咸濟其令問，三后馳光於萬葉，君子榮其輝，小人服其義。

translations.literal: Some were enlightened across different ages, so the four worthies all aided their fair fame, the three later rulers sent glory through ten thousand leaves—gentlemen gloried in their radiance, petty men submitted to their righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus worthies shine through ages and all men honor them.

sentences.zh: 今陛下尊英雄之高軌，振逸世之奇聲，何至仍衰世之異議，以掩賢人之名哉！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty honors the high track of heroes and stirs the wondrous fame of an exceptional age—how could you still follow the different opinions of a declining age to cover the names of worthy men!
translations.idiomatic: Why follow a bad age's slander and hide a worthy man's name?

sentences.zh: 若王之中外不明，終始蹈德，臣懼方今之人，不復為善矣。

translations.literal: If the Prince's inner and outer conduct is not clear and from beginning to end he treads in virtue, your servant fears people of today will no longer do good.
translations.idiomatic: If his virtue stays hidden, who will dare do good hereafter?

sentences.zh: 且世之興衰，何代無有，今齊苗裔萬世之後，其能無汙隆乎？

translations.literal: Moreover the rise and fall of ages—which generation lacks it? Can the descendants of Qi after ten thousand generations be without decline and ascent?
translations.idiomatic: Every age rises and falls; Qi's heirs too will know fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 苟前良可廢，何以勸後之能者。

translations.literal: If former worthies may be discarded, how may one encourage those able to come after?
translations.idiomatic: If past worthies are cast aside, how can later men be urged to virtue?

sentences.zh: 伏願上同周、漢、西晉之如彼，下為來胤垂範之如此。

translations.literal: I prostrate my hope that above you may match Zhou, Han, and Western Jin in that, and below set an example for coming generations like this.
translations.idiomatic: Match Zhou, Han, and Jin above; teach posterity below.

sentences.zh: 儻能降明詔，箋枉道，使往王得洗謗議，拯冥魂，賜以王禮反葬，則民之從義，猶若回風之卷草也。

translations.literal: If you could lower a bright edict and lift the wronged from the road, so that the former Prince may wash away slander, rescue his dark soul, and be granted princely rites and reburial, then the people's following righteousness would be like whirlwind rolling grass.
translations.idiomatic: Clear his name, grant princely burial, and the people will turn like grass in wind.

sentences.zh: 臣聞鸛鳴臯垤，則降陰吐雨；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the crane cries on the marsh the yin descends and rain is spit;
translations.idiomatic: When the crane cries, rain follows;

sentences.zh: 騰蛇聳躍，而沈雲鬱冥。

translations.literal: when the flying serpent rears and leaps, deep clouds are gloomy and dark.
translations.idiomatic: when the serpent rises, clouds darken.

sentences.zh: 但傷臣言輕落毛，身如橫芥，神高聽邈，終焉莫省，直欲內不負心，庶將來知王之意耳。

translations.literal: Only your servant grieves that his words fall light as shed hair, his body is like a weed across the path, the spirit high and hearing far—at the end none will understand; he only wishes not to fail his heart within, hoping that hereafter men will know the Prince's intent.
translations.idiomatic: My words are slight, yet I speak so posterity may know his heart.

sentences.zh: 又不省。

translations.literal: Again, it was not examined.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the court did not examine it.

sentences.zh: 至今上即位，乃下詔曰：「宋建平王劉景素，名父之子，少敦清尚。

translations.literal: When the present emperor ascended the throne, he then issued an edict saying, "Liu Jingsu, Prince of Jianping of Song, was the son of an illustrious father and from youth was devoted to pure and lofty conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the present emperor took the throne, he issued an edict: "Liu Jingsu, Prince of Jianping of Song, was the son of an illustrious father and was devoted from youth to pure and lofty conduct.

sentences.zh: 雖末路失圖，而原心有本。

translations.literal: Although at the end of his course he lost his plan, when one traces his heart it had a foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Though at the end he lost his way, the heart behind it had its grounds.

sentences.zh: 年流運改，宜弘優澤，可聽以王禮還葬舊墓。」

translations.literal: Years have flowed and fortune has changed; it is fitting to extend generous favor, and he may be permitted to be returned and buried in his old tomb with the rites of a prince."
translations.idiomatic: Years have passed and fortune has changed. It is fitting to extend generous favor; let him be returned and buried in his old tomb with the rites of a prince."

sentences.zh: 晉熙王昶字休道，文帝第九子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jinxi, Chang, courtesy name Xiudao, was the ninth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jinxi, Chang, courtesy name Xiudao, was Emperor Wen's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，年十歲，封義陽王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, when he was ten, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 22, at ten, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，為輔國將軍、南彭城下邳二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he became General Who Supports the State and Administrator of the two commanderies of Southern Pengcheng and Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he became General Who Supports the State and Administrator of Southern Pengcheng and Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the chief criminal murdered the ruler and set himself up, Chang was additionally made Cavalier Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief criminal committed regicide and took the throne, Chang was additionally made Cavalier Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐祚，遷太常，出為東中郎將、會稽太守，尋監會稽、東陽、臨海、永嘉、新安五郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Chang was transferred to Chamberlain for Ceremonials, sent out as General of the Gentlemen of the Household for the East and Administrator of Kuaiji, and soon supervised military affairs in the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, Chang became Chamberlain for Ceremonials, then was sent out as General of the Gentlemen of the Household for the East and Administrator of Kuaiji, soon supervising military affairs in Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，立東揚州，拜昶為刺史，東中郎將如故，進號後將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, Eastern Yang Province was established, and Chang was appointed its inspector, with General of the Gentlemen of the Household for the East as before, and was advanced in title to General of the Rear.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 1, Eastern Yang Province was established and Chang was appointed its inspector, retaining General of the Gentlemen of the Household for the East and advancing to General of the Rear.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，徵為祕書監，領驍騎將軍，加散騎常侍，遷中軍將軍、南彭城下邳二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, he was summoned to be Director of the Palace Library, concurrently General of Agile Cavalry, additionally Cavalier Regular Attendant, and was transferred to General of the Central Army and Administrator of the two commanderies of Southern Pengcheng and Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 1 he was summoned as Director of the Palace Library, concurrently General of Agile Cavalry, additionally Cavalier Regular Attendant, and then transferred to General of the Central Army and Administrator of Southern Pengcheng and Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 又出為都督江州郢州之西陽豫州之新蔡晉熙三郡諸軍事、前將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also sent out as Commander of All Military Affairs in Jiang Province, Xiyang of Ying Province, and the three commanderies of Xincai and Jinxi of Yu Province, General of the Front, and Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was also sent out as commander of military affairs in Jiang Province, Xiyang of Ying Province, and the Xincai and Jinxi commanderies of Yu Province, serving as General of the Front and Inspector of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 三年，徵為護軍將軍，給鼓吹一部，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was summoned as General Who Protects the Army, given one band of drums and pipes, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was summoned as General Who Protects the Army, given a drum-and-pipe band, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 轉中書令，中軍將軍，尋以本號開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，太常。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Army, and soon, with his original title, opened office with the same ceremonies as the Three Excellencies, and was additionally Cavalier Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Army, and soon, under his original title, opened office with the same ceremonies as the Three Excellencies, while also serving as Cavalier Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 從世祖南巡，坐斥皇太后龍舟，免開府，尋又以加授。

translations.literal: He accompanied Shizu on a southern tour, and because he had denounced the empress dowager's dragon boat, he was stripped of Opening Office; soon afterward it was again granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Shizu on a southern tour and was stripped of Opening Office for criticizing the empress dowager's dragon boat; soon afterward it was restored.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，出為使持節、都督徐兗南兗青冀幽六州豫州之梁郡諸軍事、征北將軍、徐州刺史，加散騎常侍，開府如故。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, Chang was sent out as Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs in the six provinces of Xu, Yan, Southern Yan, Qing, Ji, and You and Liang Commandery of Yu Province, General Who Campaigns North, and Inspector of Xu Province, and was additionally Cavalier Regular Attendant, with Opening Office as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Chang was sent out as Envoy Holding the Staff and commander over Xu, Yan, Southern Yan, Qing, Ji, You, and Liang Commandery of Yu, serving as General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xu Province; he was additionally Cavalier Regular Attendant, with Opening Office as before.

sentences.zh: 昶輕訬褊急，不能祗事世祖，大明中常被嫌責；

translations.literal: Chang was frivolous, scornful, narrow, and hasty; he could not respectfully serve Emperor Xiaowu and in the Daming era was often suspected and reproved;
translations.idiomatic: Chang was rash and disrespectful to Emperor Xiaowu and often fell under suspicion in Daming;

sentences.zh: 民間喧然，常云昶當有異志。

translations.literal: among the people the talk was loud, often saying Chang would have a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: People commonly said he harbored other designs.

sentences.zh: 永光、景和中，此聲轉甚。

translations.literal: In the Yongguang and Jinghe eras this talk grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The rumor grew in Yongguang and Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 廢帝既誅群公，彌縱狂悖，常語左右曰：「我即大位來，遂未嘗戒嚴，使人邑邑。」

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor having executed the high lords grew more wildly perverse and often said to his attendants: 'Since I took the great position I have never once held vigil, which makes men uneasy.'
translations.idiomatic: After killing the lords, the Deposed Emperor grew still more reckless and perverse, and often said to his attendants: "Since I took the throne, I have never once held a night watch, which leaves people uneasy."

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭誅後，昶表入朝，遣典籤蘧法生銜使。

translations.literal: After Prince Jiangxia Yigong was executed, Chang memorialized to enter court and sent the Registrar Qu Fasheng bearing the mission.
translations.idiomatic: After Yigong's death Chang asked to attend court and sent Qu Fasheng.

sentences.zh: 帝謂法生曰：「義陽與太宰謀反，我正欲討之，今知求還，甚善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor told Fasheng: 'Yiyang and the Grand Regent plot rebellion; I was just about to punish them—now knowing they ask to return, very good.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Fasheng: 'Yiyang plots with the Grand Regent; I was about to strike—good that he comes.'

sentences.zh: 又屢詰問法生：「義陽謀反，何故不啟？」

translations.literal: He also repeatedly questioned Fasheng: 'Yiyang plots rebellion—why did you not report it?'
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Fasheng: 'Why did you not report the plot?'

sentences.zh: 法生懼禍，叛走還彭城。

translations.literal: Fasheng feared disaster, rebelled and fled back to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fasheng fled in fear back to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 帝因此北討，親率眾過江。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore marched north to punish him and personally led the host across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched north in person.

sentences.zh: 法生既至，昶即聚眾起兵。

translations.literal: When Fasheng arrived, Chang immediately gathered the masses and raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chang rose as soon as Fasheng arrived.

sentences.zh: 統內諸郡，竝不受命，斬昶使。

translations.literal: All the commanderies within his jurisdiction alike refused orders and beheaded Chang's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery refused him and killed his envoys.

sentences.zh: 將佐文武，悉懷異心。

translations.literal: The aides and civil and military officers all harbored other minds.
translations.idiomatic: His officers all turned against him.

sentences.zh: 昶知其不捷，乃夜與數十騎開門北奔索虜，棄母妻，唯攜愛妾一人，作丈夫服，亦騎馬自隨。

translations.literal: Chang knew he could not succeed and at night with several dozen horsemen opened the gate and fled north to the Northern Wei, abandoning mother and wife, taking only one beloved concubine, dressed as a man, also riding and following.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing defeat, he fled north to Wei with one concubine, abandoning family.

sentences.zh: 昶家還都，二妾各生一子。

translations.literal: Chang's household returned to the capital; the two concubines each bore a son.
translations.idiomatic: His concubines at home each bore a son.

sentences.zh: 時太宗已即位，名長者曰思遠，小者曰懷遠，尋竝卒。

translations.literal: By then Taizong had already taken the throne; the elder was named Siyuan, the younger Huaiyuan; soon both died.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong named the boys Siyuan and Huaiyuan; both soon died.

sentences.zh: 追封懷遠為池陽縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Huaiyuan was posthumously enfeoffed Marquis of Chiyang with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyuan was posthumously made Marquis of Chiyang.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，以第六皇子燮字仲綏繼昶，改昶封為晉熙王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi the sixth imperial son Xie, courtesy name Zhongsui, succeeded Chang; Chang's enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi Prince Xie succeeded Chang as Prince of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 燮襲爵，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: Xie inherited the rank with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Xie received three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 太宗既以燮繼昶，乃下詔曰：「夫虎狼護子，猴猨負孫，毒性薄情，亦有仁愛，故識念氣類，尚均群品，況在人倫，可忘天屬。

translations.literal: Taizong, since Xie succeeded Chang, then issued an edict: 'Tigers and wolves protect their young, monkeys and gibbons carry their grandchildren—though their nature is thin in feeling, they also have benevolent love; therefore knowing and remembering their kind, they still balance among species—how much more in human relations can one forget heaven's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong issued an edict: "Tigers and wolves protect their young, and monkeys and gibbons carry their grandchildren. Even creatures poisonous in nature and thin in feeling have love, and so, knowing and remembering their own kind, they are still equal among all species; how much more, among human relations, can one forget Heaven-given kinship?

sentences.zh: 晉熙太妃謝氏，沈刻無親，物理罕比，征北公雖孝道無替，而遭此不慈，自少及長，闕恩鞫之□，乃至休否莫關，寒溫不訪，晨昏屏塞，定省靡因。

translations.literal: The late Imperial Consort of Jinxi, Lady Xie, was harsh and without kin, rarely matched in nature; though the Prince of the North in filial conduct was not lacking, he met this unkindness—from youth to age lacking nurture and correction, even in sickness and health she did not inquire, cold and warmth she did not visit, morning and evening she blocked him, fixed visits were denied.
translations.idiomatic: The late Imperial Consort of Jinxi, Lady Xie, was harsh and without kinship, rarely matched in nature. Though the Duke Who Campaigns North never failed in filial conduct, he met with this unkindness. From youth to adulthood he lacked the kindness of nurture; even his welfare did not concern her, she did not ask after his cold or warmth, and morning and evening access was blocked, with no way to make the regular visits.

sentences.zh: 事無違忤，動致誚責，毒句發口，人所難聞，加惡備苦，過於讎隙，遂事憤於宗姻，義傷於行路。

translations.literal: In matters without disobedience she moved to reproof; poisonous words left her mouth that men could hardly hear; added bitterness and prepared cruelty exceeded enmity—thus affairs stirred anger in the clan, righteousness was wounded in passersby.
translations.idiomatic: Even when there was no disobedience, her every act brought rebuke; poisonous words came from her mouth that people could hardly bear to hear. Her added cruelty and complete bitterness went beyond enmity, until the affair angered the clan and wounded the sense of passersby.

sentences.zh: 公故妃郗氏，婦禮無違，逢此嚴酷，遂以憂卒，用夭盛年。

translations.literal: The Prince's former consort Lady Chi observed women's rites without fault yet met this severity and therefore died of grief, cutting short her flourishing years.
translations.idiomatic: The duke's former consort, Lady Chi, did not violate a wife's rites, yet meeting this severity, she died of grief and her flourishing years were cut short.

sentences.zh: 又謝氏食則豐珍，衣則文麗，奉己之餘，播覃群下；

translations.literal: Again Lady Xie in eating had rich delicacies, in clothing ornate brocade; beyond sustaining herself she spread to the crowd below;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Lady Xie ate rich delicacies and wore patterned finery, and what remained after serving herself she spread among those below;

sentences.zh: 而諸孫纊不溫體，食不充饑，付於姏妳之手，縱以任軍之路。

translations.literal: yet the grandsons had cotton not warming the body, food not filling hunger, handed to nurses' hands and left on the road of military assignment.
translations.idiomatic: yet the grandsons had padding that did not warm their bodies and food that did not fill their hunger; they were handed over to nurses and left to the route of military assignment.

sentences.zh: 遇其所生，弃若糞土，繿縷比於重囚，窮困過於下使。

translations.literal: Meeting those she had borne she cast them aside like dung and soil; rags compared to heavy prisoners, want surpassing the lowest servants.
translations.idiomatic: Those born from her own line she cast aside like dung; in rags they were like heavily punished prisoners, and in poverty they were worse off than the lowest servants.

sentences.zh: 誠皇規方遠，沙塞將一，公脩短不諱，亦難豫圖。

translations.literal: Truly the imperial rule looks far and the desert frontiers will be unified—the Prince's length of life cannot be hidden and is hard to foresee beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the imperial plan reaches far and the frontier lands will be made one; the duke's lifespan cannot be spoken of in advance and is hard to foresee.

sentences.zh: 兼妾女累弱，一弟領主，防閑之道，人理斯急。

translations.literal: Moreover the concubines' daughters were weak; one younger brother held a fief—the way of guarding and restraining, human reason is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his concubines and daughters are weak, and one younger brother holds the fief; in the way of guarding and restraining, human principle makes this urgent.

sentences.zh: 朕所以詔第六子燮奉公為胤，欲以毗整一門，為公繼紹。

translations.literal: We therefore decree the sixth son Xie to succeed the Prince, wishing thereby to shore up the whole household and continue for the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I ordered the sixth son, Xie, to serve as the duke's heir, wishing thereby to support and order the whole household and continue the duke's succession.

sentences.zh: 但謝氏待骨肉至親，尚相棄蔑，況以義合，免苦為難。

translations.literal: But Lady Xie toward flesh-and-bone kin still treated with abandonment and scorn—how much more where bond is by righteousness would suffering be hard to avoid.
translations.idiomatic: But if Lady Xie abandoned and scorned even her closest blood kin, then where the bond is only one of duty, avoiding suffering would be difficult.

sentences.zh: 患萌防漸，危機須斷，便可還其本家，削絕蕃秩。」

translations.literal: When trouble sprouts, guard against its gradual growth; the dangerous opening must be cut off. She may at once return to her original family and be severed from princely rank."
translations.idiomatic: When trouble sprouts, guard against its gradual growth; the dangerous opening must be cut off. She may at once return to her original family and be severed from princely rank."

sentences.zh: 先是，改謝氏為射氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lady Xie had been changed to the She clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier her clan name had been changed to She.

sentences.zh: 時主幼時艱，宗室寡弱。

translations.literal: At the time the ruler was young, the times were difficult, and the imperial clan was few and weak.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the ruler was young, the times were difficult, and the imperial clan was thin and weak.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年，燮年四歲，以為使持節、監郢州豫州之西陽司州之義陽二郡諸軍事、征虜將軍、郢州刺史，以黃門郎王奐為長史，總府州之任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui, when Xie was four, he was made Envoy Holding the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Ying Province, Xiyang of Yu Province, and the two commanderies of Yiyang in Si Province, General Who Campaigns Against Caitiffs, and Inspector of Ying Province; Wang Huan, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, was made his senior clerk and managed the duties of the command and province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 1, when Xie was four, he was made Envoy Holding the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Ying Province, Xiyang of Yu Province, and Yiyang of Si Province, General Who Campaigns Against Caitiffs, and Inspector of Ying Province. Wang Huan, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, served as senior clerk and managed the command and province.

sentences.zh: 明年，太尉、江州刺史桂陽王休範舉兵逼朝廷，燮遣中兵參軍馮景祖襲尋陽，休範留中兵參軍毛惠連、州別駕程罕之居守，開門詣景祖降。

translations.literal: The next year, Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, Grand Marshal and Inspector of Jiang Province, raised troops and pressed the court. Xie sent Army Aide Feng Jingzu to attack Xunyang. Xiufan had left Army Aide Mao Huilian and provincial Biejia Cheng Hanzhi to guard it, and they opened the gates and surrendered to Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, Grand Marshal and Inspector of Jiang Province, raised troops against the court. Xie sent Feng Jingzu to attack Xunyang; Mao Huilian and Cheng Hanzhi, left behind to guard it, opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進燮號安西將軍，加督江州諸軍事，復昶所生謝氏為晉熙國太妃。

translations.literal: Xie was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the West and additionally commanded all military affairs in Jiang Province; Lady Xie, who had given birth to Chang, was restored as Grand Consort of the Jinxi state.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West and given command of Jiang Province military affairs; Lady Xie, Chang's mother, was restored as Grand Consort of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 四年，又進燮鎮西將軍，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Xie was further advanced to General Who Guards the West and given one band of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, Xie was advanced to General Who Guards the West and given a drum-and-pipe band.

sentences.zh: 順帝即位，徵為使持節、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、撫軍將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, Xie was summoned to be Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs in Yang and Southern Xu provinces, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun took the throne, Xie was summoned as Envoy Holding the Staff, commander of Yang and Southern Xu military affairs, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊世子為燮安西長史，行府州事，時亦被徵為左衞將軍，與燮俱下。

translations.literal: Before this, the Heir of Qi had served as Xie's senior clerk as General Who Pacifies the West and had conducted the affairs of the command and province; at this time he too was summoned as General of the Left Guard and went down together with Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the Heir of Qi had served as Xie's senior clerk under his Anxi command and handled the command and provincial business. He too was summoned as General of the Left Guard and went down with Xie.

sentences.zh: 會荊州刺史沈攸之舉兵反，世子因奉燮鎮尋陽之盆城，據中流，為內外形援。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi, Inspector of Jing Province, raised troops in rebellion, the heir thereupon escorted Xie to garrison Pencheng at Xunyang, occupying the midstream and forming mutual support between inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi, Inspector of Jing Province, rebelled, the heir escorted Xie to garrison Pencheng at Xunyang, holding the midstream as support between inside and outside.

sentences.zh: 攸之平，燮還京邑。

translations.literal: After Youzhi was pacified, Xie returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzhi was pacified, Xie returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 齊王為南徐州，燮解督南徐，進督南豫、江州諸軍事，進號中軍將軍、開府儀同三司，遷司徒。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi took Southern Xu Province, Xie was relieved of command over Southern Xu, advanced to command all military affairs in Southern Yu and Jiang provinces, advanced in title to General of the Central Army and Opening Office with the Same Ceremonies as the Three Excellencies, and transferred to Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qi took Southern Xu Province, Xie gave up command over Southern Xu and was advanced to command Southern Yu and Jiang military affairs. He was promoted to General of the Central Army, Opening Office with the Same Ceremonies as the Three Excellencies, and then Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，解司徒，降封陰安縣侯，食邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Xie was relieved as Minister over the Masses and reduced in rank to Marquis of Yinan County, with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, Xie was removed as Minister over the Masses and demoted to Marquis of Yinan County, with fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 謀反，賜死。

translations.literal: He plotted rebellion and was ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted rebellion and was ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 始安王休仁，文帝第十二子也。

translations.literal: Xiuren, Prince of Shian, was the twelfth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren, Prince of Shian, was Emperor Wen's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年，年十歲，立為建安王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, when he was ten, he was established as Prince of Jian'an, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 29, at ten, he was established as Prince of Jian'an with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，為祕書監，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian, he became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Colonel of Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 3 he became Director of the Palace Library and Colonel of Infantry.

sentences.zh: 尋都督南兗徐二州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he became Commander of All Military Affairs in Southern Yan and Xu provinces, Champion General, and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he commanded military affairs in Southern Yan and Xu, serving as Champion General and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，入為侍中，領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, he entered court as Palace Attendant and concurrently General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 1 he entered court as Palace Attendant and General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為湘州刺史，加散騎常侍，加號平南將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was sent out as Inspector of Xiang Province, additionally Cavalier Regular Attendant, and additionally titled General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was sent out as Inspector of Xiang Province, additionally Cavalier Regular Attendant, and titled General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷使持節、督江州南豫州之晉熙新蔡郢州之西陽三郡諸軍事、安南將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to Envoy Holding the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Jiang Province, Jinxi and Xincai of Southern Yu Province, and Xiyang of Ying Province, General Who Pacifies the South, and Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he became Envoy Holding the Staff, supervising military affairs in Jiang Province, Jinxi and Xincai of Southern Yu, and Xiyang of Ying, while serving as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 未拜，徙為散騎常侍、太常，又不拜。

translations.literal: Before taking office, he was transferred to Cavalier Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and again did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office, he was transferred to Cavalier Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for Ceremonials, and again did not take office.

sentences.zh: 仍為護軍將軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was then made General Who Protects the Army, with Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made General Who Protects the Army, retaining Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝永光元年，遷領軍將軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongguang under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was transferred to General Who Commands the Army, with Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongguang 1 under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was transferred to General Who Commands the Army, retaining Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，又遷使持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州諸軍事、安西將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，未之任，留為散騎常侍、護軍將軍，又加特進、左光祿大夫，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe, he was again transferred to Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs in Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, and Inspector of Yong Province. Before taking the post, he was kept as Cavalier Regular Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, and was also granted Specially Advanced and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness on the Left, with one band of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe 1 he was again transferred as Envoy Holding the Staff and commander over Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, with the posts General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man, and Inspector of Yong Province. Before taking the post, he was retained as Cavalier Regular Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, and was additionally made Specially Advanced and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness on the Left, with a drum-and-pipe band.

sentences.zh: 時廢帝狂悖無道，誅害群公，忌憚諸父，並囚之殿內，毆捶凌曳，無復人理。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor was wildly perverse without the Way, executed the high lords, dreaded and feared the various uncles, and imprisoned them all in the palace, beating and dragging them without human reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor imprisoned and tortured his uncles.

sentences.zh: 休仁及太宗、山陽王休祐，形體竝肥壯，帝乃以竹籠盛而稱之，以太宗尤肥，號為「豬王」，號休仁為「殺王」，休祐為「賊王」。

translations.literal: Xiuren, Taizong, and Prince Shanyang Xiuyou—all their bodies were fat and strong; the Emperor then put them in bamboo cages and weighed them; because Taizong was especially fat he was called 'Prince Pig,' Xiuren 'Killing Prince,' Xiuyou 'Thief Prince.'
translations.idiomatic: He caged his fat uncles and mocked Taizong as 'Prince Pig,' Xiuren as 'Killing Prince,' Xiuyou as 'Thief Prince.'

sentences.zh: 以三王年長，尤所畏憚，故常錄以自近，不離左右。

translations.literal: Because the three princes were older he feared them especially and therefore often kept them near himself, never leaving his side.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the three eldest princes at his side in fear.

sentences.zh: 東海王禕凡劣，號為「驢王」，桂陽王休範、巴陵王休若年少，故竝得從容。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Donghai was vulgar and inferior, called 'Prince Donkey'; Prince Xiufan of Guiyang and Prince Xiuruo of Baling were young and therefore all were treated with some ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yi of Donghai he mocked as 'Prince Donkey'; the younger princes fared somewhat better.

sentences.zh: 嘗以木槽盛飯，內諸雜食，攪令和合，掘地為坑穽，實之以泥水，裸太宗內坑中，和槽食置前，令太宗以口就槽中食，用之為歡笑。

translations.literal: He once put food in a wooden trough with various mixed foods, stirred to combine, dug a pit in the ground, filled it with mud and water, stripped Taizong naked and put him in the pit, placed the mixed trough-food before him, and made Taizong eat from the trough with his mouth, taking this as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He forced Taizong naked into a mud pit and made him eat slop from a trough for sport.

sentences.zh: 欲害太宗及休仁、休祐前後以十數，休仁多計數，每以笑調佞諛悅之，故得推遷。

translations.literal: He wished to kill Taizong and Xiuren and Xiuyou more than ten times; Xiuren was full of stratagems and each time with flattery and fawning pleased him, and therefore was promoted.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to kill Taizong and others repeatedly; Xiuren flattered his way to safety.

sentences.zh: 常於休仁前使左右淫逼休仁所生楊太妃，左右並不得已順命，以至右衛將軍劉道隆，道隆歡以奉旨，盡諸醜狀。

translations.literal: He often before Xiuren had his attendants force the Prince's birth mother Lady Yang, the attendants all unable to refuse; even Right Guard General Liu Daolong gladly obeyed and performed every vile act.
translations.idiomatic: He forced Xiuren to watch the violation of his mother; even generals obeyed.

sentences.zh: 時廷尉劉矇妾孕，臨月，迎入後宮，冀其生男，欲立為太子。

translations.literal: At that time the concubine of Minister of Justice Liu Meng was pregnant, near term, and was brought into the rear palace in hope she would bear a son to be established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Meng's pregnant concubine was taken to the palace hoping for an heir.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗忤旨，帝怒，乃裸之，縛其手腳，以杖貫手腳內，使人檐付太官，曰：「即日屠豬。」

translations.literal: Taizong once offended and the Emperor was angry; he stripped him, bound hands and feet, ran a staff through hands and feet, had men carry him to the Imperial Kitchen, saying: 'Slaughter the pig today.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once offended the emperor, who became angry, stripped him, bound his hands and feet, ran a staff through them, and had men carry him to the Imperial Kitchen, saying: "Slaughter the pig today."

sentences.zh: 休仁笑謂帝曰：「豬今日未應死。」

translations.literal: Xiuren laughed and told the Emperor: 'The pig ought not die today.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren joked: 'The pig should not die today.'

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，休仁曰：「待皇太子生，殺豬取其肝肺。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked why; Xiuren said: 'Wait until the crown prince is born, then kill the pig for his liver and lungs.'
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'Wait for the crown prince, then take the pig's liver.'

sentences.zh: 帝意乃解，曰：「且付廷尉。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was eased and he said: 'For now hand him to the Minister of Justice.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger then eased, and he said: "For now hand him to the Minister of Justice."

sentences.zh: 一宿出之。

translations.literal: After one night he released him.
translations.idiomatic: He was freed the next day.

sentences.zh: 帝將南遊荊、湘二州，明旦欲殺諸父便發。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to tour Jing and Xiang provinces; the next morning he planned to kill the various uncles and then set out.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to tour the south and kill his uncles first.

sentences.zh: 其夕，太宗克定禍難，殞帝於華林園。

translations.literal: That night Taizong settled the calamity and the Emperor died in Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: That night Taizong seized power and the emperor died at Hualin.

sentences.zh: 休仁即日推崇太宗，便執臣禮。

translations.literal: Xiuren that same day supported Taizong and at once performed the rites of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren backed Taizong at once.

sentences.zh: 明旦，休仁出住東府。

translations.literal: The next morning Xiuren went out to lodge at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Xiuren moved to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 時南平，廬陵敬先兄弟，為廢帝所害，猶未殯殮，休仁、休祐同載臨之，開帷歡笑，奏鼓吹往反，時人咸非焉。

translations.literal: At that time the brothers Jingxian of Nanping and Jingxian of Luling, killed by the Deposed Emperor, had not yet been buried; Xiuren and Xiuyou rode together to view them, opened the curtains and laughed, played martial pipes going and returning—men of the time all condemned this.
translations.idiomatic: They laughed at the unburied princes their nephew had killed.

sentences.zh: 先是，廢帝進休仁為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Earlier the Deposed Emperor had advanced Xiuren to General of Agile Cavalry and privilege equal to the Three Excellencies, his Regular Attendancy unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor had nearly made Xiuren grand minister.

sentences.zh: 未拜，太宗令書以為使持節、侍中、都督揚、南徐二州諸軍事、司徒、尚書令、揚州刺史，加班劍二十人，給三望十五乘。

translations.literal: Before he accepted, Taizong ordered in writing that he be Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, commander of Yang and Southern Xu, Minister of Works, Director of the Masters of Writing, Inspector of Yangzhou, with twenty halberd-bearers and fifteen three-canopied carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong made him commander of Yang with full honors.

sentences.zh: 時劉道隆為護軍，休仁請求解職，曰：「臣不得與此人同朝。」

translations.literal: At that time Liu Daolong was Protector of the Army; Xiuren asked to be relieved, saying: 'Your servant cannot serve in the same court as this man.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Daolong was Protector of the Army; Xiuren requested release from office, saying: "Your servant cannot serve in the same court as this man."

sentences.zh: 上乃賜道隆死。

translations.literal: The Emperor then granted Daolong death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Daolong executed.

sentences.zh: 尋諸方逆命，休仁都督征討諸軍事，增班劍三十人。

translations.literal: Soon rebellion arose in all quarters; Xiuren was made commander of punitive campaigns with thirty more halberd-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions followed; Xiuren commanded campaigns with added honors.

sentences.zh: 出據虎檻，進據赭圻。

translations.literal: He went out to hold Hujian and advanced to hold Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: He held Hujian and Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 尋領太子太傅，揔統諸軍，隨宜應接。

translations.literal: Soon he took the post of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and overall commanded the armies, responding as fit.
translations.idiomatic: He became crown prince's tutor and commanded all armies.

sentences.zh: 中流平定，休仁之力也。

translations.literal: The midstream was pacified—Xiuren's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The mid-Yangzi was pacified by his effort.

sentences.zh: 初行，與蘇侯神結為兄弟，以求神助。

translations.literal: At the first march he bonded with Lord Su as brothers to seek divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: He sought help from the spirit of Lord Su.

sentences.zh: 及事平，太宗與休仁書曰：「此段殊得蘇侯兄弟力。」

translations.literal: When affairs were settled Taizong wrote to Xiuren: 'This affair owed much to the brothers of Lord Su.'
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Taizong wrote to Xiuren: "In this matter we especially gained the strength of Lord Su and his brother."

sentences.zh: 增休仁邑四千戶，固辭，乃受千戶。

translations.literal: Xiuren's fief was increased by four thousand households; he firmly declined and accepted one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His fief grew by a thousand households after he declined more.

sentences.zh: 上流雖平，薛安都據彭城，招引索虜，復都督北討諸軍事，又增邑三千戶，不受。

translations.literal: Though the upper stream was pacified, Xue Andu held Pengcheng and drew in the Northern Wei; Xiuren was again commander of northern campaigns and his fief was increased three thousand households—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu held Pengcheng; Xiuren declined further fief increase.

sentences.zh: 時豫州刺史殷琰據壽陽，未平。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector of Yuzhou Yin Yan held Shouyang and was not yet pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan still held Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 晉平王休祐先督征討諸軍事，休祐出領江陵，休仁代督西討諸軍事。

translations.literal: Prince Xiuyou of Jinping had first commanded the punitive armies; Xiuyou went out to govern Jiangling and Xiuren replaced him as commander of western campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren replaced Xiuyou in the western command.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，進都督豫、司二州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi he was advanced to command Yu and Si provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi he added Yu and Si provinces.

sentences.zh: 休仁年與太宗鄰亞，俱好文籍，素相愛友。

translations.literal: Xiuren was near in age to Taizong; both loved literature and from of old were friendly.
translations.idiomatic: He and Taizong were peers who loved books and were close.

sentences.zh: 及廢帝世，同經危難，太宗又資其權譎之力。

translations.literal: In the Deposed Emperor's time they shared danger; Taizong also relied on his crafty strength.
translations.idiomatic: They survived the Deposed Emperor together; Taizong used his cunning.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，四方逆命，兵至近畿，休仁親當矢石，大勳克建，任緫百揆，親寄甚隆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi rebellion arose in all quarters and troops reached the suburbs; Xiuren personally faced arrows and stones, great merit was achieved, he was entrusted with the hundred offices, favor was very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taishi he won great merit at the capital's gates.

sentences.zh: 朝野四方，莫不輻湊。

translations.literal: Court, countryside, and all four directions none did not converge on him.
translations.idiomatic: All the realm flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 上漸不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor gradually was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 休仁悟其旨，其冬，表解揚州，見許。

translations.literal: Xiuren understood his intent; that winter he memorialized to relinquish Yangzhou and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren sensed danger and gave up Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，進位太尉，領司徒，固讓，又加漆輪車、劍履。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced to Grand Marshal and retained Minister of Works; he firmly declined; lacquered wheel carriage and sword at court were added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made Grand Marshal and declined again.

sentences.zh: 太宗末年，多忌諱，猜害稍甚，休仁轉不自安。

translations.literal: In Taizong's later years there were many taboos; suspicion and harm grew somewhat; Xiuren turned uneasy himself.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong grew suspicious; Xiuren grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 及殺晉平王休祐，憂懼彌切。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiuyou of Jinping was killed, worry and fear grew extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou's death deepened his fear.

sentences.zh: 其年，上疾篤，與楊運長等為身後之計，慮諸弟強盛，太子幼弱，將來不安。

translations.literal: That year the Emperor's illness was grave; with Yang Yunchang and others he made plans for after death, fearing the younger brothers' strength, the crown prince's youth, and future unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Taizong feared strong princes and a child heir.

sentences.zh: 運長又慮帝宴駕後，休仁一旦居周公之地，其輩不得秉權，彌贊成之。

translations.literal: Yunchang also feared that after the Emperor's death Xiuren might occupy the Duke of Zhou's position and their faction could not hold power, and urged it all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang urged killing Xiuren lest he rule as regent.

sentences.zh: 上疾嘗暴甚，內外莫不屬意於休仁，主書以下，皆往東府休仁所親信，豫自結納，其或直不得出者，皆恐懼。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's illness often grew suddenly severe, inside and outside all set their hopes on Xiuren; from chief clerks down all went to Xiuren's trusted men in the Eastern Palace and beforehand joined themselves; those who could not go out were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: All courtiers looked to Xiuren; his faction grew.

sentences.zh: 上既宿懷此意，至是又聞物情向之，乃召休仁入見。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long harbored this intent; now hearing that popular feeling turned to Xiuren, he summoned Xiuren to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the court favored Xiuren, Taizong summoned him.

sentences.zh: 既而又謂曰：「夕可停尚書下省宿，明可早來。」

translations.literal: Then he also said: 'Tonight you may lodge below the Masters of Writing; come early tomorrow.'
translations.idiomatic: Then he again said: "Tonight you may stay overnight below the Department of State Affairs; tomorrow you may come early."

sentences.zh: 其夜，遣人齎藥賜休仁死，時年三十九。

translations.literal: That night he sent men bearing poison to grant Xiuren death. He was thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was poisoned, aged thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上寢疾久，內外隔絕，慮人情有同異，自力乘輿出端門。

translations.literal: The Emperor had been ill long, inside and outside cut off; fearing that feelings might differ, he forced himself to ride in the imperial carriage out the Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Though ill, Taizong rode out to show control.

sentences.zh: 休仁死後，乃詔曰：「夫無將之誅，諒惟通典，知咎自引，實有偏介。

translations.literal: After Xiuren's death he issued an edict: 'The punishment of none who plot against their lord is indeed the constant canon; knowing guilt and taking blame upon oneself truly has partial grounds.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiuren's death, he issued an edict: "The punishment of those who plot against their lord is indeed a common canon; to know one's guilt and draw blame upon oneself truly has a special ground.

sentences.zh: 劉休仁地屬密親，位居台重，朕友寄特深，寵秩兼茂。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuren by land was close kin, by position heavy at the terrace; Our friendship was especially deep, favor and rank together abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuren was close kin by place, held an important position in the court, and my friendship and trust in him were especially deep, while favor and rank were both abundant.

sentences.zh: 不能弘贊國猷，裨宣政道，而自處相任，妄生猜嫌，側納群小之說，內懷不逞之志，晦景蔽跡，無事陽愚。

translations.literal: He could not expand and praise the state's plan or assist and proclaim the way of government, but placed himself in mutual trust, vainly bred suspicion, secretly received the talk of petty men, inwardly harbored unfulfilled will, hid his traces in shadow, feigning stupidity in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: He could not broadly aid the state's plans or help proclaim the way of government, but, while set in a position of mutual trust, recklessly bred suspicion, secretly accepted the words of petty men, inwardly harbored unfulfilled ambitions, and hid his traces in shadow, pretending foolishness without cause.

sentences.zh: 因近疾患沉篤，內外憂悚，休仁規逼禁兵，謀為亂逆。

translations.literal: Because of recent illness sinking deep, inside and outside were anxious; Xiuren plotted to press the forbidden troops and scheme rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Because my recent illness became grave, and inside and outside were anxious, Xiuren planned to press the palace troops and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朕曲推天倫，未忍明法，申詔誥礪，辨覈事原。

translations.literal: We bent the heavenly kinship and did not bear to apply the clear law, repeatedly admonishing and instructing to examine the origins.
translations.idiomatic: I bent the law out of heavenly kinship and could not bear to make the law plain; I repeatedly issued edicts of warning and examined the source of the affair.

sentences.zh: 休仁慚恩懼罪，遽自引決。

translations.literal: Xiuren, ashamed of grace and fearing guilt, hastily took his own decision.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren, ashamed of grace and afraid of guilt, hastily took his own life.

sentences.zh: 追尋悲痛，情不自勝，思屈法科，以申矜悼。

translations.literal: Seeking and pursuing, grief could not be overcome; thinking to bend the legal code to express pity.
translations.idiomatic: When I seek back over it, grief is more than I can bear, and I think to bend the legal statutes in order to express pity and mourning.

sentences.zh: 可宥其二子，并全封爵。

translations.literal: His two sons may be pardoned and their enfeoffments wholly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons may be pardoned, and their fiefs and titles may both be preserved.

sentences.zh: 但家國多虞，釁起台輔，永尋既往，感慨追深。」

translations.literal: But the state and family have many troubles, and misfortune arose from a chief minister; when I forever seek back over what has passed, feeling and sighing only deepen."
translations.idiomatic: But the state and family have many troubles, and misfortune arose from a chief minister; when I forever seek back over what has passed, feeling and sighing only deepen."

sentences.zh: 有司奏曰：「臣聞明罰無親，情屈於司綱，國典有經，威申於義滅。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized: 'Your servant has heard that bright punishment has no favorites, feeling bends to the director of laws; the state canon has constants, authority extends in righteous extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized: "Your servants have heard that clear punishment has no kin, and private feeling yields to the law; the state's code has constants, and authority is extended when righteousness destroys kinship.

sentences.zh: 是以梁、趙之誅，跣出稱過，來言之罰，克入致動。

translations.literal: Therefore the punishments of Liang and Zhao, barefoot, proclaimed their fault; the punishment of Lai, entering, caused movement.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, in the punishments of Liang and Zhao, men went out barefoot and confessed their faults; in the penalty for Lai's words, he was able to enter and set things in motion.

sentences.zh: 謹案劉休仁苞蓄禍跡，事蔽於天明，竄匿沉姦，情宣於民聽。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining Liu Xiuren, he harbored traces of disaster, affairs hidden from heavenly clarity, concealed deep treachery, feelings proclaimed in popular hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining Liu Xiuren, he stored up traces of disaster, with affairs hidden from Heaven's brightness, and concealed deep treachery, with his feelings proclaimed in what the people heard.

sentences.zh: 自以屬居戚近，早延恩睦，異禮殊義，望越常均。

translations.literal: Considering himself kin near the emperor, early extended favor and closeness, with different rites and special meaning, hope surpassing the constant norm.
translations.idiomatic: He considered himself a close relative, long extended favor and intimacy, and with special rites and exceptional meaning, his expectations exceeded the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 往歲授鉞南討，本非才命，啟行濃湖，特以親攝，仰遵廟略，俯藉眾效，屬承泰運，竊附成勳，而亟叨天功，多自臧伐。

translations.literal: In former years receiving the axe for southern campaign was not his talent or mandate; setting out at Dense Lake was especially because of kinship leading—looking up to follow the temple strategy, bending to borrow the multitude's effect, opportunely riding the great fortune, secretly attaching to achieved merit, yet repeatedly usurping heaven's merit and much self-praise.
translations.idiomatic: In past years, when he received the axe to campaign south, it was not because of his talent or command; when he set out from Nonghu, it was especially because kinship placed him in charge. Looking up, he followed the ancestral strategy; looking down, he relied on the efforts of the many. Meeting a fortunate time, he attached himself to completed merit, yet repeatedly usurped Heaven's achievement and often praised himself.

sentences.zh: 既聖明御宇，躬覽萬機，百司有紀，官方無越，而休仁矜勳怙貴，自謂應揔朝權，遂妄生疑難，深自猜外。

translations.literal: Now the sage illuminates the realm and personally views the ten thousand affairs; the hundred offices have discipline, officials without overstepping—yet Xiuren prized merit and relied on nobility, considering himself fit to overall hold court power, and vainly bred difficulty and suspicion, deeply guessing outward.
translations.idiomatic: Once the sagely and enlightened ruler governed the realm and personally oversaw all affairs, the hundred offices had order and official duties did not overstep; yet Xiuren boasted of merit and relied on nobility, thinking he should control court power, and so recklessly bred doubts and deeply set himself apart in suspicion.

sentences.zh: 故司空晉平刺王休祐，少無令業，長滋貪暴，蒞任陝荊，毒流西夏，編戶嗟散，列邑彫虛，聖澤含弘，未明正憲。

translations.literal: The former Minister of Works Prince Xiuyou of Jinping from youth had no fine conduct, in age ever nourished greed and violence; holding Shaanxi and Jing, poison flowed in western Xia, registered households sighed and scattered, listed towns were carved empty—the sage grace was inclusive and the correct law was not yet clarified.
translations.idiomatic: The late Minister of Works, Prince Xiuyou of Jinping, had no good conduct when young and grew more greedy and violent as he aged. When he held office in Shan and Jing, his poison flowed through the western regions; registered households sighed and scattered, and cities were carved empty. The sagely grace was broad and generous, and the correct law had not yet been made clear.

sentences.zh: 亟與休仁論其愆跡，辭意既密，不宜傳廣，遂飾容旨，反相勸激。

translations.literal: Repeatedly with Xiuren discussing his faults, the words were already secret and should not be spread widely—yet he adorned his countenance and contrary to this urged and incited.
translations.idiomatic: I repeatedly discussed his faults with Xiuren, and because the wording and meaning were secret, they should not have been spread widely; yet he dressed up his expression and intent and instead encouraged and stirred him.

sentences.zh: 休祐以休仁位居朝右，任遇優崇，必能為己力援，故深相黨結。

translations.literal: Xiuyou because Xiuren stood at the court's right with favor and honor supreme thought he must aid his own force and therefore deeply joined factions.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou, because Xiuren held a high position at court and received exceptional treatment, believed he could surely act as a powerful support for him, and therefore they formed a deep factional bond.

sentences.zh: 休祐於是輸金薦寶，承顏接意，造膝之間，必論朝政，遂無日不俱行，無時不同宿，聲酣聚集，密語清閒。

translations.literal: Xiuyou then offered gold and recommended treasures, received his expression and met his intent; between steps to the knee they must discuss court government—there was no day not walking together, no time not sleeping together, voices drunk in gathering, secret words in quiet leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou then sent gold and offered treasures, matching his expression and meeting his intent. In close conversation they invariably discussed court government; there was no day when they did not go together, no time when they did not stay together, drinking and gathering noisily, and speaking secretly in quiet leisure.

sentences.zh: 休仁含姦扇惑，善於計數，說休祐使外托專慎之法，密行貪詐之心，謂朝廷不覺，人莫之悟。

translations.literal: Xiuren harbored treachery and fanned delusion, skilled in calculation, urging Xiuyou outwardly to rely on exclusive caution, inwardly to practice greedy fraud, saying the court did not notice and men did not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren harbored treachery and fanned delusion, and was good at calculation. He told Xiuyou outwardly to adopt a method of exclusive caution while secretly carrying out a heart of greed and fraud, saying that the court would not notice and that no one would understand.

sentences.zh: 休祐遂乃外積怨懼，內協禍心，既得贊激，凶慝轉熾，與休仁共為姦謀，潛伺機隙，圖造釁變，規肆凶狡。

translations.literal: Xiuyou then outwardly accumulated resentment and fear, inwardly joined a treacherous heart; having obtained praise and incitement, fierce wickedness turned hotter; with Xiuren he shared treacherous plans, secretly watched for openings, plotted to make trouble and change, scheming to display fierce cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou then outwardly accumulated resentment and fear, inwardly joined a heart of disaster, and once he had obtained praise and incitement, his wickedness grew still fiercer. Together with Xiuren he made treacherous plans, secretly watched for openings, plotted to create upheaval, and planned to indulge his fierce cunning.

sentences.zh: 休仁致殞倉卒，實維天誅，而晉平國太妃妾邢不能追慚子惡，上感曲恩，更懷不逞，巫蠱祝詛。

translations.literal: Xiuren's sudden death was truly heaven's punishment; yet the Jinping state's late consort concubine Xing could not pursue shame for her son's evil, above moved by partial grace, again harbored unfulfilled will, witchcraft and curse-prayer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren's sudden death was truly Heaven's punishment; yet Lady Xing, concubine of the former Grand Consort of the Jinping state, could not feel shame for her son's evil, was moved above by partial grace, again harbored unfulfilled ambitions, and practiced witchcraft and curses.

sentences.zh: 休仁因聖躬不和，猥謀姦逆，滅道反常，莫斯為甚，殛肆朝市，庶申國刑，而法網未加，自引厥命。

translations.literal: Xiuren because the sage person was unwell vilely plotted treachery, extinguishing the Way and reversing constants—nothing surpasses this; execution in the market should declare the state punishment, yet the law net was not applied and he took his own fate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren took advantage of the sagely body's illness to plot vile treason; no destruction of the Way or reversal of the constant is worse than this. He should have been executed and exposed in the court market, so that the state's punishment might be declared, but before the net of law was applied, he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 天慈矜厚，減法崇恩，賜全二息，及其爵封，斯誠弘風曠德，貫絕通古，然非所以棄惡流釁，懲懼亂臣者也。

translations.literal: Heaven's kindness was thick and reduced the law to exalt grace, granting both sons and their noble enfeoffments—this is truly vast wind and far virtue, penetrating through antiquity—yet it is not thereby to abandon evil and spread misfortune or warn rebellious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly kindness, pitying and generous, reduced the law and exalted grace, granting the preservation of his two sons and their titles and fiefs. This is truly a vast custom and broad virtue, surpassing all past and present, yet it is not the way to abandon evil, let guilt flow on, and make rebellious ministers afraid.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，謂宜追降休仁為庶人，絕其屬籍，見息悉徙遠郡。

translations.literal: Your servants jointly propose that Xiuren should be posthumously reduced to commoner, his genealogy severed, surviving sons all moved to distant commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants have discussed this and say Xiuren should be posthumously reduced to commoner, his clan register cut off, and his surviving sons all moved to distant commanderies.

sentences.zh: 休祐愆謀始露，亦宜裁黜，徙削之科，一同舊准。

translations.literal: Xiuyou's treacherous plan just exposed should also be punished and moved; the penalty of exile and reduction should follow the old standard.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiuyou's wrongful plan has only now been exposed, he too should be punished and reduced; the statutes for exile and reduction should all follow the old standard.

sentences.zh: 收邢付獄，依法窮治。」

translations.literal: Seize Xing and deliver her to prison; according to law, investigate fully."
translations.idiomatic: Seize Xing and deliver her to prison; according to law, investigate fully."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「邢匹婦狂愚，不足與計。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Xing, a common woman's madness and stupidity, is not worth accounting.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "Xing is a mad and foolish common woman, not worth taking into account.

sentences.zh: 休仁知釁自引，情有追傷，可特為降始安縣王，食邑千戶，并停伯融等流徙，聽襲封爵。

translations.literal: Xiuren knowing guilt took blame himself; feeling has pursuing injury—specially reduce to Prince of Shian with one thousand households, and stop Borong and others' exile, permitting inheritance of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren knew the guilt and drew it upon himself; in feeling there is lingering grief. He may specially be reduced to Prince of Shian with a fief of one thousand households, and the exile of Borong and the others is to be stopped, permitting them to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 伯猷先紹江夏國，令還本，賜爵鄉侯。」

translations.literal: Boyou had earlier succeeded to the Jiangxia state; order him returned to his original line and grant him the rank of district marquis."
translations.idiomatic: Boyou had earlier succeeded to the Jiangxia state; order him returned to his original line and grant him the rank of district marquis."

sentences.zh: 上既殺休仁，慮人情驚動，與諸方鎮及諸大臣詔曰：

translations.literal: The Emperor having killed Xiuren, fearing popular feelings would be shaken, with the various frontier commanders and high ministers issued an edict:
translations.idiomatic: Taizong explained Xiuren's death to the generals:

sentences.zh: 休仁致殞，卿未具悉，事之始末，今疏以相示。

translations.literal: Xiuren's death—you have not fully understood; the affair from beginning to end is now set forth to show you.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the full story to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 休祐貪恣非政，法網之所不容。

translations.literal: Xiuyou's greedy lawlessness was what the legal net could not tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou's greed broke the law.

sentences.zh: 昔漢梁孝王、淮南厲王無它釁悖，正以越漢制度耳。

translations.literal: Formerly Han's Prince Xiao of Liang and Prince Li of Huainan had no other misdeeds or perversity—only because they exceeded Han institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Han princes fell only for overstepping ritual.

sentences.zh: 況休祐吞嚼聚斂，為西數州之蝗，取與鄙虐，無復人情。

translations.literal: How much more Xiuyou's swallowing and gathering—locusts of several western provinces; taking and giving was base and cruel, without human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou was a plague on the western provinces.

sentences.zh: 屢得王景文、褚淵、沈攸之等啟，陳其罪惡，轉不可容。

translations.literal: Repeatedly receiving memorials from Wang Jingwen, Chu Yuan, Shen Youzhi, and others stating his crimes, it turned impossible to tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials denounced him.

sentences.zh: 吾篤兄弟之恩，不欲致之以法，且每恨大明兄弟情薄，親見休祐屯苦之時，始得寬寧，彌不忍問。

translations.literal: Our deep brotherly feeling did not wish to bring him under law; moreover each time we resented the thin feeling among Daming's brothers—personally seeing Xiuyou's bitter distress, when he first obtained ease we could not bear to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Brotherly love delayed punishment.

sentences.zh: 所以改授徐州，冀其去朝廷近，必應能自悛革。

translations.literal: Therefore we transferred him to Xuzhou, hoping that near the court he would surely reform himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Xuzhou to reform.

sentences.zh: 及拜徐州，未及之任，便徵動萬端，暴濁愈甚，既每為民蠹，不可復全。

translations.literal: On receiving Xuzhou, before reaching the post he stirred ten thousand affairs; violent filth grew worse; having long been vermin to the people, he could not be preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: He grew worse in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 休仁身粗有知解，兼為宰相；

translations.literal: Xiuren was coarse but had some understanding and was also chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren was clever and chief minister;

sentences.zh: 又吾與其兄弟情昵，特復異常，頗與休仁論休祐釁狀。

translations.literal: again Our feeling with his brothers was intimate, especially exceptional; we often discussed Xiuyou's misdeeds with Xiuren.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong discussed Xiuyou with Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 休祐以休仁為吾所親，必應知吾意；

translations.literal: Xiuyou thought Xiuren was one We favored and would surely know Our intent;
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou thought Xiuren knew the emperor's mind;

sentences.zh: 又云休仁言對，能為損益。

translations.literal: also saying Xiuren's words in reply could add or subtract.
translations.idiomatic: and that Xiuren could sway the throne.

sentences.zh: 遂多與財賂，深相結事，乃寢必同宿，行必共車。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gave much gold and silk and deeply joined in affairs; they must sleep together and ride the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou bribed him and stayed always at his side.

sentences.zh: 休仁性軟，易感說，遂成繾綣，共為一家，是吾所吐密言，一時倒寫。

translations.literal: Xiuren's nature was soft and easily persuaded; they became bound tight and were one household—this was Our confidential speech, all at once poured out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren repeated the emperor's secrets to Xiuyou.

sentences.zh: 吾與休仁，少小異常，唯虛心信之，初不措疑。

translations.literal: Our feeling with Xiuren from youth was exceptional; We only trusted him with open heart and at first set no suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had trusted Xiuren blindly.

sentences.zh: 雖爾猶慮清閒之時，非意脫有聞者。

translations.literal: Even so We still feared that in quiet leisure something might accidentally be heard.
translations.idiomatic: He still feared leaks.

sentences.zh: 吾近向休祐推情，戒訓嚴切，休祐更不復致疑。

translations.literal: We recently pushed feeling toward Xiuyou with stern admonition; Xiuyou no longer dared suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: A final warning was given Xiuyou.

sentences.zh: 休祐死後，吾將其內外左右，問以情狀，方知言語漏泄并具之由，彌日懊惋，心神萎孰。

translations.literal: After Xiuyou's death We questioned his inner and outer attendants on the circumstances and then knew the reason speech leaked and was fully reported; day-long regret, spirit and mind withered.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiuyou died Taizong learned Xiuren had betrayed confidences.

sentences.zh: 休仁又說休祐云：「汝但作佞，此法自足安。

translations.literal: Xiuren also told Xiuyou: 'You need only act the flatterer—this method is enough for safety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren also told Xiuyou: "You need only act the flatterer; this method is enough for safety.

sentences.zh: 我常秉許為家，從來頗得此力。

translations.literal: I always hold favor for the family and from of old have quite gained this force.
translations.idiomatic: I have always held this as a method for the family, and from the beginning I have gained much strength from it.

sentences.zh: 但試用，看有驗不？」

translations.literal: Just try using it, and see whether it proves effective."
translations.idiomatic: Just try using it, and see whether it proves effective."

sentences.zh: 休祐從之，於是大有獻奉，言多乖實，積惡既不可恕。

translations.literal: Xiuyou followed this; thereupon there was great offering and tribute, words mostly departing from truth, accumulated evil already unpardonable.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou flattered and bribed until unpardonable.

sentences.zh: 自休祐殞亡之始，休仁款曲共知。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Xiuyou's death Xiuren's intimate sharing was fully known.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiuyou's death, Xiuren knew everything.

sentences.zh: 休仁既無罪釁，主相本若一體，吾之推意，初無有間。

translations.literal: Xiuren had no guilt or fault; lord and minister were originally as one body—Our pushing feeling at first had no gap.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren was innocent; emperor and minister had been one.

sentences.zh: 休祐貪愚，為天下所疾，致殞之本，為民除患，兄弟無復多人，彌應思弔不咸，益相親信。

translations.literal: Xiuyou was greedy and foolish, detested by all under Heaven; the root of his death was removing harm for the people—brothers were not many more; we should think of mourning and not salt, and increase mutual trust.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou was killed for the people's good; kin should draw closer.

sentences.zh: 休祐平生，狼抗無賴，吾慮休仁往哭，或生祟禍。

translations.literal: Xiuyou all his life was wolfish and unbridled; We feared that if Xiuren went to mourn, some calamity might arise.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong feared mourning might cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 且吾爾日本辦仗往哭，晚定不行。

translations.literal: Moreover that day We had prepared arms to go mourn but in the evening decided not to go.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to mourn but did not.

sentences.zh: 吾所以為設方便，呼入在省。

translations.literal: We therefore made a convenience and summoned him into the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Xiuren to the Secretariat instead.

sentences.zh: 而休仁得吾召入，大自驚疑，遂入辭楊太妃，顏色狀意，甚與常異。

translations.literal: When Xiuren received Our summons he was greatly startled and suspicious; he then went to take leave of Lady Yang, his color and expression very unlike the usual.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren, alarmed, visited his mother before going.

sentences.zh: 既至省，楊太妃驟遣監子去來參察。

translations.literal: Having reached the Secretariat, Lady Yang suddenly sent a supervising son back and forth to observe.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang sent spies to watch.

sentences.zh: 從此日生嫌懼，而吾之推情，初不疑覺。

translations.literal: From this day suspicion and fear arose, while Our pushing feeling at first did not suspect or perceive.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong did not yet suspect him.

sentences.zh: 從休祐死後，吾再幸休仁第，飲噉極日，排閤入內，初無猜防，休仁坐生嫌畏。

translations.literal: After Xiuyou's death We twice visited Xiuren's mansion, eating and drinking all day, pushing aside screens to enter the inner rooms—at first without suspicion or guard; Xiuren sat and bred suspicion and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Visits that once seemed friendly now frightened Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 一日，吾春中多期射雉，每休仁清閒，多往雉場中，或敕使陪輦，及不行日，多不見之。

translations.literal: One day in spring We often set dates for shooting pheasants; whenever Xiuren was free We often went to the pheasant field, or ordered him to accompany the carriage; on days We did not go he was often not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's hunting visits made Xiuren anxious.

sentences.zh: 每值宵，休仁輒語左右云：「我已復得今一日。」

translations.literal: Each time night came Xiuren would tell his attendants: 'I have won one more day.'
translations.idiomatic: Each night Xiuren would tell his attendants: "I have won one more day."

sentences.zh: 及在房內見諸妓妾，恆語：「我去不知朝夕見底，若一旦死去作鬼，亦不取汝，取汝正足亂人耳。」

translations.literal: And seeing the singing girls in his rooms he always said: 'I do not know when I will see the bottom of day; if one morning I die a ghost I will not take you—you would only trouble men.'
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the singers and concubines in his rooms, he would always say: "I do not know whether I will see the end by morning or evening. If one day I die and become a ghost, I still will not take you; taking you would only be enough to trouble people."

sentences.zh: 休祐死時，日已三晡，吾射雉，始從雉場出，休仁從騎在右，伏野中，吾遣人召之，稱云：「腹痛，不堪騎馬。」

translations.literal: When Xiuyou died the sun was already in the third watch; We were shooting pheasants and had just left the field; Xiuren's mounted escort was on the right, lying hidden in the wild; We sent men to summon him and he claimed: 'Belly pain, cannot ride.'
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuyou died, the day was already late afternoon. I was shooting pheasants and had just left the pheasant grounds; Xiuren's riders were on the right, hidden in the fields. I sent someone to summon him, and he claimed: "My belly hurts; I cannot ride a horse."

sentences.zh: 爾時諸王車皆停在朱雀門裏，日既暝，不暇遠呼車，吾衣書車近在離門裏，敕呼來，下油幢絡，擬以載之。

translations.literal: At that time all the princes' carriages stopped inside the Vermilion Bird Gate; the day was already dark and there was no time to call distant carriages; Our book carriage was near inside the Li Gate; We ordered it called, lowered the oil canopy, intending to carry him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent his own carriage for him.

sentences.zh: 吾由來諳悉其體有冷患，聞腹痛，知必是冷，乃敕太醫上省送供御高梁薑飲以賜之。

translations.literal: We from of old knew well his body had a cold ailment; hearing belly pain, knew it must be cold, and ordered the Imperial Physician to the Secretariat to send imperial sorghum-ginger drink to grant him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent ginger drink for his 'cold.'

sentences.zh: 休仁得飲，忽大驚，告左右稱：「敗今日了。」

translations.literal: Xiuren having received the drink suddenly was greatly alarmed and told his attendants: 'Ruined—today is finished.'
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuren received the drink, he suddenly became greatly alarmed and told his attendants: "Today is ruined."

sentences.zh: 左右答曰：「此飲是御師名封題。」

translations.literal: The attendants answered: 'This drink is sealed by the imperial physician by name.'
translations.idiomatic: The attendants answered: "This drink is sealed with the name of the imperial physician."

sentences.zh: 休仁乃令左右先飲竟，猶不甚信，乃僶俛噬之，裁進一合許。

translations.literal: Xiuren then ordered attendants to drink it all first; still not greatly believing, he bent and sipped it, barely one he entering.
translations.idiomatic: He made others taste it first, then sipped barely.

sentences.zh: 妄生嫌貳，事事如是。

translations.literal: Vainly bred suspicion and division—every affair was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Everything fed his paranoia.

sentences.zh: 由來十日五日，一就問太妃。

translations.literal: Formerly every ten or five days he once inquired after the late consort.
translations.idiomatic: He used to visit his mother regularly.

sentences.zh: 自休祐死後，每吾詔，必先至楊太妃問，如分別狀。

translations.literal: After Xiuyou's death, each time We summoned him he must first go to Lady Yang and inquire, as if distinguishing.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiuyou's death he always visited Lady Yang before court.

sentences.zh: 休仁由來自營府國興生文書，二月中，史承祖齎文書呈之，忽語承祖云：「我得成許那，何煩將來。」

translations.literal: Xiuren from of old himself managed the fief state's revenue documents; in the second month Shi Chengzu brought documents to present; suddenly he told Chengzu: 'I have achieved that much—why trouble to bring them?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren had always personally managed the fief state's revenue documents. In the second month, Shi Chengzu brought the documents and presented them, and Xiuren suddenly told Chengzu: "I have obtained this much; why trouble to bring them?"

sentences.zh: 吾虛心如舊，不復見信，既懷不安，大自嫌恐，惟以情理，不容復有善心。

translations.literal: Our open heart was as before but he no longer saw trust; already harboring unease, greatly self-suspicious and fearful—only by reason and feeling could he not again have good will.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's trust was gone; Xiuren despaired.

sentences.zh: 休仁既經南討，與宿衛將帥經習狎共事相識者，佈滿外內。

translations.literal: Xiuren having passed through the southern campaign, with garrison generals long familiar from close service, filled inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: His southern campaign made him popular with guards.

sentences.zh: 常日出入，於廂下經過，與諸相識將帥，都不交言。

translations.literal: On ordinary days going out and in, passing below the side chambers, with familiar generals he did not exchange words at all.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped greeting guard officers.

sentences.zh: 及吾前者積日失適，休仁出入殿省，諸衛主帥裁相悉者，無不和顏厚相撫勞。

translations.literal: When We before had been unwell for accumulated days, Xiuren going in and out of the palace halls—with commanders of the guards he was even slightly acquainted—none did not receive him with harmonious faces and thick comfort.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizong was ill, Xiuren courted the guards.

sentences.zh: 爾時吾既甚惡，意不欲見外人，悠悠所傳，互言差劇。

translations.literal: At that time We were very ill and did not wish to see outsiders; vague reports passed mutually saying better or worse.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong hid his illness; rumors spread.

sentences.zh: 休仁規欲聞知方便，使曇度道人及勞彥遠屢求啟，闞覘吾起居。

translations.literal: Xiuren schemed to hear conveniently and had the monk Tandu and Lao Yanyuan repeatedly seek audience, peering at Our daily routine.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents to spy on the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 及其所啟，皆非急事，吾意亦不厝疑。

translations.literal: What they reported was not urgent affairs; Our mind also did not set suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong still did not suspect those reports.

sentences.zh: 吾與休仁，親情實異，年少以來，恆相追隨，情向大趣，亦往往多同，難否之日，每共契闊。

translations.literal: Our kin feeling with Xiuren was truly different; from youth we always followed each other; emotional direction in great matters also often much alike—in hard or easy days we often shared together.
translations.idiomatic: They had been close since youth.

sentences.zh: 休仁南討為都統，既有勳績，狀之於心，亦何極已。

translations.literal: Xiuren in the southern campaign as overall commander had merit; to state it in the heart, how could it be extreme!
translations.idiomatic: His southern merit was real.

sentences.zh: 但休仁於吾，望既不輕，小人無知，亦多挾背向，既生猜貳，不復自寧。
