translations.literal: But Xiuren's hope toward Us was not light; petty men without knowledge also mostly carried backs turned; once suspicion and division arose he could not again be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet suspicion and flatterers destroyed peace.

sentences.zh: 夫禍難之由，皆意所不悟，如其意趣，人莫能測，事不獲已，反覆思惟，不得不有近日處分。

translations.literal: The source of calamity and difficulty—all are what the mind does not awaken to; as for his intent, men cannot measure; the affair could not be helped; turning and rethinking, we could not but have the recent disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster came unawares; execution was unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 夫於兄弟之情，不能無厚薄。

translations.literal: In brotherly feeling, thick and thin cannot be without.
translations.idiomatic: Brotherly love is not equal.

sentences.zh: 休祐之亡，雖復悼念，猶可以理割遣；

translations.literal: Xiuyou's death, though again mourned, could still be cut off by reason;
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou's death could be borne with reason;

sentences.zh: 及休仁之殞，悲愍特深，千念不能已已，舉言傷心。

translations.literal: but Xiuren's demise—grief and pity especially deep, a thousand thoughts cannot cease, every word wounds the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren's death grieved Taizong far more.

sentences.zh: 事之細碎，既不可曲載詔文，恐物不必即解，兼欲存其兒子，不欲窮法。

translations.literal: Matters minute and fragmented cannot be bent to load the edict; fearing men might not understand at once, and also wishing to preserve his sons, not wishing to exhaust the law.
translations.idiomatic: The public edict could not tell all; sons were spared.

sentences.zh: 為詔之辭，不得不云有兵謀，非事實也。

translations.literal: The edict's wording could not but say there was military plotting—it is not the fact.
translations.idiomatic: The charge of military plot was not true.

sentences.zh: 故相報卿知。

translations.literal: Therefore reporting to you, sir, to know.
translations.idiomatic: This is told so you may know.

sentences.zh: 上與休仁素厚，至於相害，慮在後嗣不安。

translations.literal: The Emperor with Xiuren from of old was thick; as to mutual harm, the worry was future descendants' unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong killed him fearing for his heir.

sentences.zh: 休仁既死，痛悼甚至，謂人曰：「我與建安年時相鄰，少便狎從。

translations.literal: After Xiuren's death grief was extreme; he told men: 'I and Jian'an in years were neighbors; from youth we were intimate.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiuren died, he mourned him with extreme grief and told people: "Jian'an and I were neighbors in our younger years and were intimate from youth.

sentences.zh: 景和、泰始之間，勳誠實重。

translations.literal: Between Jinghe and Taishi, loyal merit was truly heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jinghe and Taishi, his merit and sincerity were truly weighty.

sentences.zh: 事計交切，不得不相除。

translations.literal: Affairs pressed and cut close—could not but mutually remove.
translations.idiomatic: The matter and plan pressed hard, and there was no choice but to remove one another.

sentences.zh: 痛念之至，不能自已。

translations.literal: Pain and remembrance to the utmost could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: When I think of him with utmost pain, I cannot stop myself.

sentences.zh: 今有一事不如與諸侯共說，歡適之方，於今盡矣。」

translations.literal: Now there is one matter that is not as good as speaking together with the princes; the way of joy and ease is, from now, exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Now there is one matter that is not as good as speaking together with the princes; the way of joy and ease is, from now, exhausted."

sentences.zh: 因流涕不自勝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept and could not overcome himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wept uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 子伯融，妃殷氏所生。

translations.literal: His son Borong—the consort Lady Yin bore him.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Borong, born of Lady Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷氏，吳興太守沖女也。

translations.literal: Lady Yin was daughter of Administrator of Wuxing Yin Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin was Yin Chong's daughter.

sentences.zh: 范陽祖翻有醫術，姿貌又美，殷氏有疾，翻入視脈，說之，遂通好。

translations.literal: Fan Yang Zu Fan had medical skill and his appearance was also beautiful; Lady Yin had illness; Fan entered to feel the pulse, won her, and they became intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Physician Zu Fan had an affair with Lady Yin.

sentences.zh: 事泄，遣還家賜死。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; he was sent home and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Fan was sent home and ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 伯融歷南豫州刺史，琅邪、臨淮二郡太守，寧朔將軍，廣州刺史，不之職。

translations.literal: Borong served as Inspector of Southern Yu, Administrator of Langye and Linhuai, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Guangzhou—he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Borong held several posts but never took Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廢徙丹楊縣。

translations.literal: He was deposed and moved to Danyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽元年，還京邑，襲封始興王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui of the Later Deposed Emperor he returned to the capital and inherited the enfeoffment as Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and became Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 弟伯猷，初出繼江夏愍王伯禽，封江夏王，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: His younger brother Boyou at first went out to succeed Prince Min of Jiangxia Boqin, enfeoffed Prince of Jiangxia with two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Boyou had succeeded Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 休仁死後還本，與伯融俱徙丹楊縣。

translations.literal: After Xiuren's death he returned to origin; with Borong he was both moved to Danyang County.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiuren's death both were exiled.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽元年，賜爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui of the Later Deposed Emperor he was granted the noble rank Marquis of the District.
translations.idiomatic: Boyou became a district marquis.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素為逆，楊運長等畏忌宗室，稱詔賜伯融等死。

translations.literal: When Prince Jingsu of Pingping rebelled, Yang Yunchang and others feared and dreaded the imperial clan; proclaiming the edict they granted Borong and others death.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang had Borong and Boyou killed in Jingsu's revolt.

sentences.zh: 伯融時年十九，伯猷年十一。

translations.literal: Borong was then nineteen; Boyou eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Borong was nineteen; Boyou eleven.

sentences.zh: 晉平剌王休祐，文帝第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Li of Jinping, Xiuyou, was the thirteenth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li of Jinping, Xiuyou, was Emperor Wen's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，年十一，封山陽王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, when he was eleven, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shanyang, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2, at eleven, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shanyang with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，為散騎常侍，領長水校尉，尋遷東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, he became Cavalier Regular Attendant and concurrently Colonel of Changshui, and was soon transferred to Inspector of Eastern Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 1 he became Cavalier Regular Attendant and Colonel of Changshui, and was soon transferred as Inspector of Eastern Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 未拜，徙湘州刺史，加號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Before taking office, he was transferred to Inspector of Xiang Province and additionally given the title General Who Campaigns Against Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office, he was transferred as Inspector of Xiang Province and given the title General Who Campaigns Against Caitiffs.

sentences.zh: 四年，還為祕書監，領右軍將軍，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he returned to become Director of the Palace Library and concurrently General of the Right Army, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he returned as Director of the Palace Library and General of the Right Army, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，又遷左中郎將，都官尚書，又為祕書監，領驍騎將軍，出為使持節、都督豫司二州南豫州之梁郡諸軍事、右將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, then to General of the Gentlemen of the Household on the Left and Minister of the Capital Bureau, then again became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently General of Agile Cavalry, and was sent out as Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs in Yu and Si provinces and Liang Commandery of Southern Yu Province, General of the Right, and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, then to General of the Gentlemen of the Household on the Left and Minister of the Capital Bureau. Later he again became Director of the Palace Library, concurrently General of Agile Cavalry, and was sent out as Envoy Holding the Staff, commander over Yu and Si provinces and Liang Commandery of Southern Yu, General of the Right, and Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，入朝，進號鎮西大將軍，仍遷散騎常侍、鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe, he entered court, was advanced in title to General-in-Chief Who Guards the West, and was then transferred to Cavalier Regular Attendant, General-in-Chief Who Guards the Army, and Opening Office with the Same Ceremonies as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe 1 he entered court, was advanced to General-in-Chief Who Guards the West, and then became Cavalier Regular Attendant, General-in-Chief Who Guards the Army, and Opening Office with the Same Ceremonies as the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 太宗定亂，以為使持節、都督荊、湘、雝、益、梁、寧、南、北秦八州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、荊州刺史，開府、常侍如故。

translations.literal: When Taizong settled the turmoil he was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of eight provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Inspector of Jingzhou, with office equal to the Three Excellencies and Regular Attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong made Xiuyou commander of eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 又改都督江、郢、雍、湘五州、江州刺史；

translations.literal: Again changed to commander of five provinces Jiang, Ying, Yong, Xiang and Inspector of Jiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted among many commands;

sentences.zh: 又改都督江、南豫、司州、南豫州刺史，改都督豫、江、司三州、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: again changed to commander of Jiang, Southern Yu, and Si and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, again commander of Yu, Jiang, and Si and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: his posts changed repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 時豫州刺史殷琰據壽陽反叛，休祐出鎮歷陽，督劉勔等討琰，琰未平，勔築長圍守之。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector of Yuzhou Yin Yan held Shouyang in rebellion; Xiuyou went out to govern Liyang and commanded Liu Yu and others to punish Yan; Yan was not yet pacified and Yu built a long encirclement to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Yin Yan at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 休祐復徙都督荊、湘、雝、益、梁、寧、南、北秦八州諸軍事、荊州刺史，持節、常侍、將軍、開府竝如故，增封二千戶，受五百戶。

translations.literal: Xiuyou was again transferred to commander of eight provinces and Inspector of Jingzhou, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, general, and office equal to the Three Excellencies all unchanged, fief increased two thousand households, accepted five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief grew while he campaigned.

sentences.zh: 以山陽荒敝，改封晉平王。

translations.literal: Because Shanyang was wild and poor, he was changed to Prince of Jinping.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned from Shanyang to Jinping.

sentences.zh: 休祐素無才能，彊梁自用，大明之世，年尚少，未得自專，至是貪淫，好財色。

translations.literal: Xiuyou by nature had no talent, was overbearing and self-willed; in the Daming era he was still young and could not act on his own—to now he was greedy, lecherous, fond of wealth and women.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was restrained; now he was greedy and lecherous.

sentences.zh: 在荊州，裒刻所在，多營財貨。

translations.literal: In Jingzhou he extorted wherever he went and much amassed wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He plundered Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以短錢一百賦民，田登，就求白米一斛，米粒皆令徹白，若有破折者，悉刪簡不受。

translations.literal: With short cash one hundred he levied the people; when the fields were harvested he demanded white rice one hu, every grain required to be fully white; if any were broken they were all culled and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded perfectly white rice at extortionate rates.

sentences.zh: 民間糴此米，一升一百。

translations.literal: Among the people buying this rice, one sheng cost one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: People paid a hundred per sheng.

sentences.zh: 至時又不受米，評米責錢。

translations.literal: At the time he also would not accept rice but assessed rice and demanded cash.
translations.idiomatic: He even demanded cash instead of grain.

sentences.zh: 凡諸求利，皆悉如此，百姓嗷然，不復堪命。

translations.literal: Every kind of seeking profit was all like this; the hundred surnames groaned and could no longer bear the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Every levy was alike; the people were ruined.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，徵為都督南徐、南兗、徐、兗、青、冀六州諸軍事、南徐州刺史，加侍中，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi he was summoned as commander of six provinces and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, plus Regular Attendant, Bearer of the Staff and general unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi he was recalled to command Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 上以休祐貪虐，不可蒞民，留之京邑，遣上佐行府州事。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Xiuyou was greedy and cruel and could not govern the people kept him in the capital and sent senior aides to conduct the prefecture and province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong kept him at court, unfit to rule.

sentences.zh: 休祐佷戾彊梁，前後忤上非一。

translations.literal: Xiuyou was perverse, overbearing, and strong; before and after he offended the Emperor not once.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly defied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 在荊州時，左右苑景達善彈棊，上召之，休祐留不遣。

translations.literal: In Jingzhou his attendant Yuan Jingda was skilled at chess; the Emperor summoned him; Xiuyou detained and did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to release a chess player the emperor wanted.

sentences.zh: 上怒，詰責之曰：「汝剛戾如此，豈為下之義！」

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and reproved him: 'You are so overbearing and perverse—how is this the righteousness of serving below!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor became angry and reproached him: "You are so hard and perverse; how can this be the proper conduct of a subordinate!"

sentences.zh: 積不能平。

translations.literal: Grievance could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Anger festered.

sentences.zh: 且慮休祐將來難制，欲方便除之。

translations.literal: Moreover fearing Xiuyou would be hard to control in future, wishing to remove him conveniently.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong planned to kill him.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，車駕於岩山射雉，有一雉不肯入場，日暮將反，令休祐射之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year the imperial carriage at Rock Mountain shot pheasants; one pheasant would not enter the field; at dusk about to return, he ordered Xiuyou to shoot it.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt Taizong ordered Xiuyou to shoot a stubborn pheasant.

sentences.zh: 語云：「不得雉，勿歸。」

translations.literal: He said: 'Without the pheasant, do not return.'
translations.idiomatic: 'No pheasant, no return.'

sentences.zh: 休祐時從在黃麾內，左右從者竝在部伍後，休祐便馳去，上遣左右數人隨之。

translations.literal: Xiuyou then followed inside the yellow awning; left and right followers were all behind the ranks; Xiuyou galloped away; the Emperor sent several men of the left to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou rode off; guards followed.

sentences.zh: 上既還，前驅清道，休祐人從悉分散，不復相得，上因遣壽寂之等諸將追之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already returned and the vanguard cleared the road; Xiuyou's men were all scattered and could not find one another; the Emperor therefore sent Shou Jizhi and various generals to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent assassins after him.

sentences.zh: 日已欲闇，與休祐相及，逼令墜馬。

translations.literal: The day was already about to darken; they caught up with Xiuyou and pressed him to fall from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk they caught him.

sentences.zh: 休祐素勇壯有氣力，奮拳左右排擊，莫得近。

translations.literal: Xiuyou by nature was brave, strong, and spirited; he swung fists left and right beating away and none could approach.
translations.idiomatic: He fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 有一人後引陰，因頓地，即共毆拉殺之。

translations.literal: One man pulled from behind in secret; he therefore fell to the ground and together they beat and strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: They pulled him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 乃遣人馳白上，行唱：「驃騎落馬。」

translations.literal: Then sent men galloping to report to the Emperor, walking and crying: 'The General of Agile Cavalry fell from his horse.'
translations.idiomatic: They reported: 'The general fell from his horse.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「驃騎體大，落馬殊不易。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'The General of Agile Cavalry's body is large—falling from a horse is especially not easy.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The General of Agile Cavalry has a large body; falling from a horse is especially not easy."

sentences.zh: 即遣御醫絡驛相係。

translations.literal: At once sent imperial physicians in relay succession.
translations.idiomatic: He sent doctors in haste.

sentences.zh: 頃之，休祐左右人至，久已絕。

translations.literal: Soon Xiuyou's attendants arrived—long already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou was already dead.

sentences.zh: 去車腳，輿以還第，時年二十七。

translations.literal: Removing the carriage shafts, they carried him on a litter back to his mansion; he was twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-seven; carried home dead.

sentences.zh: 追贈司空，持節、侍中、都督、刺史如故，給班劍二十人，三望車一乘。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, commander, and inspector unchanged, twenty halberd-bearers, one three-canopied carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he kept his titles and honors.

sentences.zh: 時巴陵王休若在江陵，其日即馳信報休若曰：「吾與驃騎南山射雉，驃騎馬驚，與直閣夏文秀馬相蹹，文秀墮地，驃騎失鞚，馬驚，觸松樹墮地，落硎中，時頓悶，不識人，故馳報弟。」

translations.literal: At that time Prince Xiuruo of Baling was in Jiangling; that day he galloped a letter reporting to Xiuruo: 'I with the General of Agile Cavalry shot pheasants at South Mountain; the general's horse was startled and collided with Direct Attendant Xia Wenxiu's horse; Wenxiu fell to the ground; the general lost his reins; the horse was startled, struck a pine and fell to the ground, dropped into a rut, for a moment was dazed and did not know people—therefore I gallop to report to you, younger brother.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Xiuruo of Baling was in Jiangling. That day he immediately sent a fast letter to Xiuruo, saying: "I was shooting pheasants with the General of Agile Cavalry at South Mountain. The general's horse was startled and collided with Direct Attendant Xia Wenxiu's horse; Wenxiu fell to the ground, the general lost the reins, the horse bolted, struck a pine tree, and threw him to the ground. He fell into a rut and for the moment was dazed and did not recognize people, so I have hurried to report this to my younger brother."

sentences.zh: 其年五月，追免休祐為庶人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he was posthumously stripped and reduced to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was posthumously demoted to commoner.

sentences.zh: 長子士薈，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son, Shihui, died early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shihui died young.

sentences.zh: 次子宣翊為世子，為寧朔將軍、湘州刺史，未拜，免廢。

translations.literal: His next son Xuanyi became heir, and was made General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and Inspector of Xiang Province, but before taking office he was dismissed and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: His next son Xuanyi became heir and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and Inspector of Xiang Province, but before he took office he was dismissed and deposed.

sentences.zh: 次士弘，繼鄱陽哀王休業，襲封，被廢還本。

translations.literal: Next was Shihong, who succeeded Prince Ai of Poyang, Xiuye, and inherited the fief; after being deposed he was returned to his original line.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Shihong, who succeeded Prince Ai of Poyang, Xiuye, and inherited that fief; when deposed, he was returned to his original line.

sentences.zh: 次宣彥，封原豐縣侯，為寧朔將軍、彭城太守，未拜，免廢。

translations.literal: Next was Xuanyan, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuanfeng County and appointed General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and Administrator of Pengcheng, but before taking office he was dismissed and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Xuanyan, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuanfeng County and appointed General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and Administrator of Pengcheng, but before taking office he was dismissed and deposed.

sentences.zh: 次宣諒。

translations.literal: Next was Xuanliang.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Xuanliang.

sentences.zh: 次宣曜，出繼南平穆王鑠封，被廢還本。

translations.literal: Next was Xuanyao, who was sent out to succeed to the fief of Prince Mu of Nanping, Shuo; after being deposed he was returned to his original line.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Xuanyao, who was sent out to inherit the fief of Prince Mu of Nanping, Shuo; when deposed, he was returned to his original line.

sentences.zh: 次宣景，次宣梵，次宣覺，次宣受，次宣則，次宣直，次宣季，凡十三子，並徙晉平郡。

translations.literal: Next were Xuanjing, Xuanfan, Xuanjue, Xuanshou, Xuanze, Xuanzhi, and Xuanji: thirteen sons in all, who were all moved to Jinping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Xuanjing, Xuanfan, Xuanjue, Xuanshou, Xuanze, Xuanzhi, and Xuanji, thirteen sons in all; all were relocated to Jinping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太宗尋病，見休祐為祟，乃遣前中書舍人劉休至晉平撫慰宣翊等，上遂崩。

translations.literal: Soon Taizong fell ill and saw Xiuyou appearing as a baleful spirit, so he sent former Secretariat Drafter Liu Xiu to Jinping to soothe and comfort Xuanyi and the others; the emperor then died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Taizong fell ill and saw Xiuyou haunting him. He sent former Secretariat Drafter Liu Xiu to Jinping to reassure Xuanyi and the others, and then the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽元年，聽宣翊等還都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor, Xuanyi and the others were permitted to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 1 under the Later Deposed Emperor, Xuanyi and the others were allowed to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明三年，謀反，並賜死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, they plotted rebellion and were all ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 3 under Emperor Shun, they plotted rebellion and were all ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽哀王休業，文帝第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Poyang, Xieye, was the fifteenth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ai of Poyang, Xieye, was Emperor Wen's fifteenth son.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，年十一，封鄱陽王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed Prince of Poyang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 2, at eleven, he became Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 三年，薨，追贈太常。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; posthumously granted Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 3; posthumously Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 大明六年，以山陽王休祐次子士弘嗣封。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming the second son of Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang, Shihong, succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong succeeded him in the sixth year of Daming.

sentences.zh: 被廢還本，國除。

translations.literal: He was deposed and returned to origin; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 臨慶沖王休倩，文帝第十六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Chong of Linqing, Xiuqian, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chong of Linqing, Xiuqian, was Emperor Wen's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，年九歲，疾篤，封東平王，食邑二千戶，未拜，薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, at age nine, gravely ill, he was enfeoffed Prince of Dongping with two thousand households; before accepting he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 1, at nine, enfeoffed Prince of Dongping but died before taking the title.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，立第二十七皇子子嗣為東平王，紹休倩後。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming the twenty-seventh imperial son Zisi was established Prince of Dongping to succeed Xiuqian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daming Prince Zisi succeeded Xiuqian as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始二年還本，國絕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi of Taizong he returned to origin and the state was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 六年，以第五皇子智丹為東平王，繼休倩，未拜，薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the fifth imperial son Zhidan was made Prince of Dongping to succeed Xiuqian; before accepting he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Prince Zhidan was named successor but died before taking the title.

sentences.zh: 其年，追改休倩為臨慶王，以臨賀郡為臨慶國，立第八皇子躋為臨慶王，食邑二千戶，繼休倩後。

translations.literal: That year posthumously Xiuqian was changed to Prince of Linqing; Linhe commandery was made the Linqing state; the eighth imperial son Ji was established Prince of Linqing with two thousand households to succeed Xiuqian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuqian was posthumously made Prince of Linqing; Prince Ji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 明年，還本國。

translations.literal: The next year he returned to his original state.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ji returned to his original rank.

sentences.zh: 休倩，太祖所愛，故前後屢加紹門嗣。

translations.literal: Xiuqian was loved by the Grand Ancestor; therefore repeatedly successors were added to the lineage.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor loved Xiuqian and repeatedly refilled his line.

sentences.zh: 新野懷王夷父，文帝第十七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Xinye, Yifu, was the seventeenth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Xinye, Yifu, was Emperor Wen's seventeenth son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年，薨，時年六歲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia he died, aged six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, aged six.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始五年，追加封諡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi of Taizong enfeoffment and posthumous title were added.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong posthumously enfeoffed him in the fifth year of Taishi.

sentences.zh: 巴陵哀王休若，文帝第十九子也。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Baling, Xiuruo, was the nineteenth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ai of Baling, Xiuruo, was Emperor Wen's nineteenth son.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，年九歲，封巴陵王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian, when he was nine, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Baling, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 3, at the age of nine, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Baling with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，為冠軍將軍、南琅邪臨淮二郡太守，徙南彭城、下邳二郡太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, he became Champion General and Administrator of the two commanderies of Southern Langye and Linhuai; he was transferred to be Administrator of the two commanderies of Southern Pengcheng and Xiapi, with his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 2 he became Champion General and Administrator of Southern Langye and Linhuai. He was then transferred to administer Southern Pengcheng and Xiapi, keeping his generalship.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為都督徐州諸軍事、徐州刺史，將軍如故，增督豫州之梁郡，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was sent out as Commander of All Military Affairs in Xu Province and Inspector of Xu Province, with his generalship as before; he was additionally given command over Liang Commandery of Yu Province, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was sent out as commander of Xu Province military affairs and Inspector of Xu Province, keeping his generalship. Liang Commandery of Yu Province was added to his command, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 明年，徵為散騎常侍、左中郎將、吳興太守。

translations.literal: The next year, he was summoned to be Cavalier Regular Attendant, General of the Gentlemen of the Household on the Left, and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned as Cavalier Regular Attendant, General of the Gentlemen of the Household on the Left, and Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 復徵為散騎常侍、太常。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Cavalier Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as Cavalier Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 未拜，前廢帝永光元年，遷左衞將軍。

translations.literal: Before taking office, in the first year of Yongguang under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office, in Yongguang 1 under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was transferred to General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始元年，遷散騎常侍、中書令，領衞尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi under Taizong, he was transferred to Cavalier Regular Attendant and Director of the Secretariat, concurrently holding the Chamberlain for the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taizong's Taishi reign, he became Cavalier Regular Attendant and Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Chamberlain for the Guards.

sentences.zh: 未拜，復為左衞將軍，常侍、衞尉如故。

translations.literal: Before taking office, he again became General of the Left Guard, with his posts as Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for the Guards as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office, he again became General of the Left Guard, retaining his posts as Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for the Guards.

sentences.zh: 又未拜，出為使持節、都督會稽東陽永嘉臨海新安五郡諸軍事、領安東將軍、會稽太守，率眾東討。

translations.literal: Again before taking office, he was sent out as Envoy Holding the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs in the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Yongjia, Linhai, and Xin'an, concurrently General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Kuaiji, and led troops east to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Again before taking office, he was sent out as Envoy Holding the Staff and commander of military affairs in Kuaiji, Dongyang, Yongjia, Linhai, and Xin'an, while holding General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Kuaiji, and led troops eastward.

sentences.zh: 進督吳、吳興、晉陵三郡。

translations.literal: He was advanced to command the three commanderies of Wu, Wuxing, and Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given command over Wu, Wuxing, and Jinling commanderies.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍，進號衞將軍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Cavalier Regular Attendant, advanced in title to General of the Guards, and given one band of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made Cavalier Regular Attendant, advanced to General of the Guards, and given a drum-and-pipe band.

sentences.zh: 又進督晉安囗囗二郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to command military affairs in Jin'an and two commanderies whose names are lacunose.
translations.idiomatic: He was further given command of military affairs in Jin'an and two commanderies whose names are lost.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵隨二郡諸軍事、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，持節、常侍、將軍如故，增邑二千戶，受三百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to military affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, and the two commanderies of Jingling and Sui in Ying Province, and became Colonel Who Pacifies the Man and Inspector of Yong Province, with Staff, Regular Attendant, and General as before; his fief was increased by two thousand households, of which he received three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was transferred to command military affairs in Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, Northern Qin, and the Ying Province commanderies of Jingling and Sui, serving as Colonel Who Pacifies the Man and Inspector of Yong Province. He retained Staff, Regular Attendant, and General, and his fief was increased by two thousand households, of which he received three hundred.

sentences.zh: 前在會稽，錄事參軍陳郡謝沈以諂佞事休若，多受賄賂。

translations.literal: Formerly in Kuaiji, Recorder Xie Shen of Chen flattered Xiuruo and received many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji, Xie Shen flattered Xiuruo and took bribes.

sentences.zh: 時內外戒嚴，普著袴褶，沈居母喪。

translations.literal: At that time inside and outside were on alert; all wore trousers and short coats; Shen was in mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court was in mourning dress, Shen was in filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 被起，聲樂酣飲，不異吉人，衣冠既無殊異，竝不知沈居喪，嘗自稱孤子，眾乃駭愕。

translations.literal: He was raised from mourning, music and wine in hearty drinking no different from a lucky man; dress had no special difference and all did not know Shen was in mourning; he once called himself 'orphan son' and the crowd was startled.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted in mourning as if at ease, shocking all.

sentences.zh: 休若坐與沈褻黷，致有姦私，降號鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Xiuruo was punished for intimacy and irreverence with Shen and for having illicit relations; reduced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo was demoted for debauchery with Shen.

sentences.zh: 又進衛將軍。

translations.literal: Again advanced to General Who Guards the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored to General Who Guards the Realm.

sentences.zh: 典籤夏寶期事休若無禮，繫獄，啟太宗殺之，慮不被許，啟未報，輒於獄行刑，信反，果錮送，而寶期已死。

translations.literal: Registrar Xia Baoqi served Xiuruo without propriety, was imprisoned; he reported to Taizong to kill him, fearing permission would not be granted; before the report returned he executed in prison; the letter returned and indeed he was shackled and sent—but Baoqi was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Baoqi executed a prisoner before imperial approval and was sent in bonds.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，與休若書曰：「孝建、大明中，汝敢行此邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angry and wrote to Xiuruo: 'In Xiaojian and Daming did you dare do this?'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote: 'Did you dare this in Xiaojian and Daming?'

sentences.zh: 休若母加杖三百，降號左將軍，貶使持節都督為監，行雝州刺史，使寧蠻校尉，削封五百戶。

translations.literal: Xiuruo's mother was additionally beaten three hundred strokes; he was reduced to General of the Left, Bearer of the Staff reduced to supervisor, acting Inspector of Yongzhou, Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, fief reduced five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was flogged; he lost rank and five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷使持節、都督湘州諸軍事、行湘州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Xiangzhou, acting Inspector of Xiangzhou, general unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was sent to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，荊州刺史晉平王休祐入，以休若監荊州事，進號征南將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Prince Xiuyou of Jinping entered as Inspector of Jingzhou; Xiuruo supervised Jingzhou affairs, advanced to General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he supervised Jingzhou and became inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 仍為都督荊、湘、雝、益、梁、寧、南、北秦八州諸軍事、征西將軍、荊州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: He was then made commander of eight provinces, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, Bearer of the Staff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded eight provinces as General Who Conquers the West.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍，又進號征西大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon plus Regular Attendant; again advanced to Grand General Who Conquers the West with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He gained Regular Attendant and Three Excellencies privilege.

sentences.zh: 七年，晉平王休祐被殺，建安王休仁見疑。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Prince Xiuyou of Jinping was killed and Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was suspected.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Xiuyou was killed and Xiuren fell under suspicion.

sentences.zh: 京邑訛言休若有至貴之表，太宗以言報之，休若內甚憂懼。

translations.literal: In the capital false talk said Xiuruo had a sign of supreme nobility; Taizong reported the words to him and Xiuruo inwardly was very fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors said Xiuruo was destined for the throne; Taizong told him, deepening his fear.

sentences.zh: 會被徵代休祐為都督南徐、南兗、徐、兗、青、冀六州諸軍事、征北大將軍、南徐州刺史，持節、常侍、開府如故。

translations.literal: He was then summoned to replace Xiuyou as commander of six provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, and office equal to the Three Excellencies unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned north to replace Xiuyou.

sentences.zh: 休若腹心將佐咸謂還朝必有大禍，中兵參軍京兆王敬先固陳不宜入，勸割據荊楚以距朝廷，休若偽許之。

translations.literal: Xiuruo's trusted generals and aides all said returning to court must bring great disaster; Army Aide Wang Jingxian of Jingzhao firmly stated he should not enter and urged seizing Jing and Chu to resist the court; Xiuruo falsely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: His aides urged rebellion; Xiuruo pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 敬先既出，執錄，馳使白太宗，敬先坐誅死。

translations.literal: When Jingxian had gone out he was seized and recorded; a fast messenger reported to Taizong; Jingxian was punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian was arrested and executed when he left.

sentences.zh: 休若至京口，建安王休仁又見害，益懷危慮。

translations.literal: Xiuruo reached Jingkou; Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was again killed; fear grew more.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkou he learned Xiuren was dead and grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 上以休若和善，能諧緝物情，慮將來傾幼主，欲遣使殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Xiuruo was kindly and could harmonize popular feelings, fearing he would overturn the young lord in future, wished to send men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong feared the gentle Xiuruo would dominate the child emperor.

sentences.zh: 慮不奉詔，徵入朝，又恐猜駭，乃偽遷休若為都督江、郢、司、廣、交、豫州之西陽、新蔡、晉熙、湘州之始興四郡諸軍事、車騎大將軍、江州刺史，持節、常侍、開府如故。

translations.literal: Fearing he would not obey the decree, summoning him to court also feared suspicion and alarm; therefore falsely transferred Xiuruo to commander of Jiang, Ying, Si, Guang, Jiao, and four commanderies of Xiyang, Xincai, Jinxi in Yu, and Shixing in Xiang, Grand Marshal and Inspector of Jiangzhou, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, office equal to the Three Excellencies unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He pretended to promote Xiuruo to Jiangzhou while planning his death.

sentences.zh: 徵還召拜，手書殷勤使赴。

translations.literal: Summoned back for appointment; handwritten letter earnest urging him to come.
translations.idiomatic: A warm summons lured him to court.

sentences.zh: 七月七日，即於第賜死，時年二十四。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month he was granted death at his mansion; he was twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: On the Double Seventh he was executed at home, aged twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、司空，持節、都督、刺史如故，給班劍二十人，三望車一乘。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Regular Attendant and Minister of Works, Bearer of the Staff, commander, and inspector unchanged, twenty halberd-bearers, one three-canopied carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received full honors.

sentences.zh: 休若既死，上與驃騎大將軍桂陽王休範書曰：

translations.literal: After Xiuruo's death the Emperor wrote to Grand General of Agile Cavalry Prince Xiufan of Guiyang:
translations.idiomatic: After Xiuruo's death Taizong wrote to Prince Xiufan of Guiyang:

sentences.zh: 外間有一師，姓徐名紹之，狀如狂病，自云為塗步郎所使。

translations.literal: Outside there is a master surnamed Xu named Shaozhi, appearing like mad illness, himself saying he is sent by the painted step lord.
translations.idiomatic: A mad seer named Xu Shaozhi claimed divine orders.

sentences.zh: 去三月中，忽云：「神語道巴陵王應作天子，汝使巴陵王密知之。」

translations.literal: In the third month suddenly he said: 'The spirit speaks that Prince of Baling should be Son of Heaven—you make Prince of Baling know secretly.'
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, he suddenly said: "The spirit says that Prince of Baling should become Son of Heaven; make Prince of Baling know this secretly."

sentences.zh: 於是師便訪覓休若左右人，不能得。

translations.literal: Thereupon the master then sought Xiuruo's attendants but could not get them.
translations.idiomatic: The seer tried to reach Xiuruo's men and failed.

sentences.zh: 東宮典書姓何者相識，數去來，師解神語，東宮典書具道神語，東宮典書答云：「我識巴陵間一左右，當為汝向道。」

translations.literal: He knew a Eastern Palace clerk surnamed He; they came and went several times; the master explained the spirit speech; the Eastern Palace clerk fully reported the spirit speech; the Eastern Palace clerk answered: 'I know one attendant of Baling— I will tell him for you.'
translations.idiomatic: He knew an Eastern Palace clerk surnamed He, who came and went several times. The master explained the spirit's words, and the Eastern Palace clerk fully reported them. The Eastern Palace clerk answered: "I know one attendant around Baling; I will tell him for you."

sentences.zh: 數日，東宮典書復來語師云：「我已為汝語巴陵左右，道因達巴陵，巴陵具知，云『莫聲，但聽。』」

translations.literal: Several days later the Eastern Palace clerk again came and told the master: "I have already told Baling's attendant for you; the word reached Baling; Baling fully knows and says, 'Do not speak; only listen.'"
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the Eastern Palace clerk again came and told the master: "I have already told Baling's attendant for you; the word reached Baling; Baling fully knows and says, 'Do not speak; only listen.'"

sentences.zh: 又頃者史官奏天文占候，頗云休若應挾異端。

translations.literal: Again recently the historiographers memorialized astronomical observation, largely saying Xiuruo should harbor heterodox intent.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers too said Xiuruo showed ominous signs.

sentences.zh: 神道芒昧，乃不可全信，然前後相准，略亦不無髣髴。

translations.literal: The spirit Way is dim and obscure and cannot be wholly trusted—yet before and after matching, roughly there is also some resemblance.
translations.idiomatic: Omens were uncertain yet suggestive.

sentences.zh: 且帖肆間，自大明以來有「若好」之謠，于今未止。

translations.literal: Moreover among posted notices, from Daming onward there has been the ballad 'ruo hao,' to now not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A ballad 'ruo hao' had circulated since Daming.

sentences.zh: 詔若百重章句，皆配以美辭美事，諸不逞之徒，咸云必是休若。

translations.literal: Edicts if layered in a hundred weight of clauses all paired with fine words and fine affairs—all the unbridled fellows said it must be Xiuruo.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels said fine edicts proved Xiuruo would rule.

sentences.zh: 休若且知道路有異音，里巷有「若好」之謠，在西已奇懼，致王敬先吐猖狂之言。

translations.literal: Xiuruo moreover knew the roads had strange sounds and the lanes had the 'ruo hao' ballad; in the west already strangely fearful, causing Wang Jingxian to spit frantic words.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo also knew that there were strange sounds on the roads and the "Ruo is good" ballad in the lanes. In the west he was already unusually afraid, leading Wang Jingxian to utter reckless words.

sentences.zh: 近休祐、休仁被誅，休若彌不自安，又左右多是不相當負罪之徒，恆說以道路之言叩動之，相與唱云：「萬民之心，屬在休若」，感激其意。

translations.literal: Recently Xiuyou and Xiuren were executed; Xiuruo more did not feel at ease; again many attendants were unfit men with guilt, constantly speaking road words to stir him, together singing: 'The ten thousand people's hearts belong to Xiuruo'—moving his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Xiuyou and Xiuren had been executed, and Xiuruo became still more uneasy. Many of those around him were also unsuitable and guilty men; they constantly used rumors from the roads to stir him, and together chanted: "The hearts of the ten thousand people belong to Xiuruo," exciting his mind.

sentences.zh: 尋休若從來心跡，殊有可嫌。

translations.literal: Seeking Xiuruo's conduct from of old, there was much to suspect.
translations.idiomatic: His past conduct was suspicious.

sentences.zh: 劉亮問高次祖，汝一應識此人，當給休若。

translations.literal: Liu Liang asked Gao Cizu: you should know this man—he should be given to Xiuruo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang assigned Cizu to Xiuruo.

sentences.zh: 休若在東縱恣群下無本末，還朝被貶，爵位小退，次祖被亮使歸，過問訊，大泣，語次祖云：「我東行是一段功，在郡橫為群小輩過失，大被貶降，我實憤怨，不解劉輔國何意不作。」

translations.literal: Xiuruo in the east indulged his subordinates without order; returning to court was demoted, noble rank slightly retreated; Cizu was sent by Liang to return, inquired and wept greatly, saying to Cizu: 'My eastern march was a stretch of merit; in the commandery I was wrongly faulted by petty fellows, greatly demoted—I truly resent and do not understand why Liu Fuguo did not act.'
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuruo was in the east, he indulged his subordinates without order; after returning to court he was demoted and his rank and position were slightly reduced. When Cizu was sent back by Liang and stopped by to ask after him, Xiuruo wept greatly and told Cizu: "My eastern journey was a stretch of merit, yet in the commandery I was arbitrarily faulted by petty men and heavily demoted. I am truly resentful and do not understand why Liu Fuguo does not act."

sentences.zh: 次祖答云：「劉輔國蒙朝廷生成之恩，豈容有此理。」

translations.literal: Cizu answered: 'Liu Fuguo receives the court's grace of life—how could there be such reason.'
translations.idiomatic: Cizu answered: "Liu Fuguo has received the court's grace of nurture and protection; how could there be such a principle?"

sentences.zh: 推此已是有奇意。

translations.literal: Pushing this, there already was strange intent.
translations.idiomatic: That alone showed strange intent.

sentences.zh: 吾使諸王在蕃，正令優游而已，本不以武事，而休若在西，廣召弓馬健兒，都不啟聞。

translations.literal: We make the various princes in the domains just to let them roam at ease; originally not for military affairs—yet Xiuruo in the west broadly summoned bowmen and horse stalwarts, none reported to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were not to arm themselves; Xiuruo secretly gathered troops.

sentences.zh: 又戾道明等，昔親為賊，罪應萬死，休若至西，大信遇之，乃潛將往不啟京。

translations.literal: Again Li Daoming and others, formerly personally rebels, guilt deserving ten thousand deaths—Xiuruo reaching the west greatly trusted and favored them and secretly led them west without reporting to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sheltered former rebels without informing court.

sentences.zh: 吾知汝意謂休若處奉因事事何如，心跡既不復可測，因其還朝在第與書，事事詰誚於內，許密自引分，狀如暴疾致故，差得於其名位及見子悉得全也。

translations.literal: We know your thought says Xiuruo in serving because of each affair how was it—the heart's traces could no longer be measured; because he returned to court at his mansion We wrote, everything interrogated and reproved within, permitting him secretly to take blame himself, appearing like sudden illness causing death—somewhat obtaining that his name and rank and visible sons were all preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: We killed him gently so his sons might live—do you think that was mercy?

sentences.zh: 休若既是汝弟，使其狼心得申者，汝得守冶城邊作太尉公邪？

translations.literal: Xiuruo is after all your younger brother—if his wolfish heart were fulfilled, could you guard the edge of Ye City as Grand Marshal?
translations.idiomatic: If Xiuruo had won, could you have remained Grand Marshal?

sentences.zh: 非但事關計，亦於汝甚切，汝可密白荀太妃令知。

translations.literal: Not only the affair concerns planning—it also cuts close to you—you may secretly report to the late Imperial Consort Gou to let her know.
translations.idiomatic: Tell the Grand Consort Gou in secret.

sentences.zh: 廬江王褘昔在西州，故上云冶城邊也。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Lujiang had formerly been in the western province; therefore the above says, "by Ye City."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Lujiang had formerly been in the western province; this is why the text above says "by Ye City."

sentences.zh: 休若子冲始襲封。

translations.literal: Xiuruo's son Chong initially inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo's son Chong initially inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明三年薨，會齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Shengming under Emperor Shun; when Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shengming 3 under Emperor Shun. When Qi received the abdication, the princely state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《詩》云：「不自我先，不自我後。」

translations.literal: The historian says: The Odes say: 'Not before me, not after me.'
translations.idiomatic: The historian cites the Odes: 'Not before me, not after me.'

sentences.zh: 古人畏亂世也。

translations.literal: The ancients feared chaotic ages.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients feared such times.

sentences.zh: 太宗晚途，疑隙內成，尋斧所加，先自至戚。

translations.literal: In Taizong's later road, suspicion and gaps formed within; where the axe and halberd were applied began with the nearest kin.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's late reign turned on kin with the axe.

sentences.zh: 晉剌以獷暴摧軀，巴哀由和良鴆體，保身之路，未知攸適。

translations.literal: Prince Jin was destroyed by fierce violence, Prince Ai of Baling by gentle goodness poisoned—the way to preserve life, unknown where to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jinping fell to violence, Baling to poison—the path of safety was gone.

sentences.zh: 昔之戒子，慎勿為善，將遠有以乎！

translations.literal: The ancients' warning to sons—careful not to do good—will it reach far?
translations.idiomatic: The old warning 'do not be good'—does it still hold?
